Created by combining 26 images taken on June 3, 2010. {{ill|GSI Aerial Photograph|ja|国土航空写真|12=draft|12=draft}}. Ōshima is located about 6.5 {{ill|kilometers|ja|キロメートル|12=draft|12=draft}} northwest of the Konominato Port on the Munakata mainland. About 5 km to the east lies {{ill|Jinoshima|ja|地島|12=draft|12=draft}}. Together with Jinoshima and {{ill|Okinoshima|ja|沖ノ島|12=draft|12=draft}}, it marks the boundary between {{ill|Genkai Sea|ja|玄界灘|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|12=draft|12=draft}}—the sea on the west side of the island is Genkai-nada, and on the east side is Hibiki-nada. Its total area is 7.17 km{{sup|2}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001015648.pdf List of Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Areas]}} – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, National and Regional Policy Bureau, Remote Islands Development Division, making it the largest of the remote islands in Fukuoka Prefecture. Much of the island is hilly with steep terrain, and the highest peak is Mitake (224 m) in the island’s center. On the eastern side of the island is Ōshima Port, where ferries connect to the mainland, and a ferry terminal is located there. Slightly south of the ferry terminal is Ōshima Fishing Port, while Miyazaki Fishing Port is to the northeast. Homes and settlements are concentrated around these port areas. The population is 540 with 278 households (from the Reiwa 2 {{ill|National Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本)|lt=National Census|lt_ja=国勢調査|12=draft|12=draft}}). The island has {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|12=draft|12=draft}}, a {{ill|compulsory education school|ja|義務教育学校|12=draft|12=draft}}. == History == In [[1889]] (Meiji 22), under the {{ill|Town and Village Act|ja|町村制|12=draft|12=draft}}, it became {{ill|Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島村 (福岡県)|lt=Oshima Village|lt_ja=大島村|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata District|ja|宗像郡|12=draft|12=draft}}. From May 27 to 28, 1905, the {{ill|Battle of Tsushima|ja|日本海海戦|12=draft|12=draft}} took place offshore, and many Russian soldiers’ bodies washed ashore on Ōshima.[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ Katsuya Kodama “Memorial Service for the Russo-Japanese War on Munakata City’s Ōshima ~A New Bridge of Friendship and Peace between Japan and Russia!~” (November 3, 2013)] (Accessed January 16, 2018) Residents are said to have buried them respectfully. On March 28, 2005, the village was merged into Munakata City. Beginning in 1935 (Shōwa 10), as part of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|12=draft|12=draft}}, a battery was constructed on the island’s northern coast (Ōshima Battery) equipped with four {{ill|Type 45 15 cm Cannon|ja|四五式十五糎加農砲|12=draft|12=draft}}. Associated facilities included an observation post, underground ammunition depot, a mobile 150 cm searchlight, and a power station. After the war, these cannons were removed, but their mounts and other remnants remain. Since 2012, a Japan–Russia joint memorial service has been held for those who died in the Battle of Tsushima, and in November 2013, a monument to the war dead was erected in front of the former Ōshima Battery. In July 2017 ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 29), Nakatsumiya and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho were inscribed as part of the “{{ill|Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|ja|「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|12=draft|12=draft}}” World Heritage Site. == Religious Facilities == At the summit of Mt. Mitake stands an observation platform and the Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) of Nakatsumiya, called {{ill|Mitake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}}. In ancient times, this was a ritual site for Nakatsumiya. Nearby is the Orihime-Hikoboshi Shrine, and local tradition holds that this place is the birthplace of Japan’s Tanabata legend. Near the port is Nakatsumiya of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}}, dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the {{ill|The Three Female Deities of Munakata|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|12=draft|12=draft}}. On the north side of the island is the {{ill|Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|ja|沖津宮遙拝所|lt=Okitsumiya Yohaisho|lt_ja=沖津宮遙拝所|12=draft|12=draft}}, where one can worship the distant island of Okinoshima, home to Okitsumiya, which is forbidden to women. On clear days, one can faintly see Okinoshima from there, but it cannot be seen on cloudy or rainy days. These two sites are part of the “Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region,” a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. Additionally, Ōshima is traditionally said to be the place where {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|12=draft|12=draft}} spent his final years in exile. It is also on the route of the {{ill|Kyushu Olle|ja|九州オルレ|12=draft|12=draft}} hiking course. == Major Facilities and Attractions on the Island == === Main Facilities === * Municipal Office – Munakata City Ōshima Administrative Center * School – {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|12=draft|12=draft}} * Nursery – Ōshima Nursery School === Tourist Attractions === * Umingu Ōshima – A marine experience facility offering {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sea kayaking|ja|シーカヤック|12=draft|12=draft}}. * {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} Nakatsumiya – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. Dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the Munakata Three Sisters. * {{ill|Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|ja|御嶽神社 (宗像市)|lt=Mitake Shrine|lt_ja=御嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}} – The Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) and original sacred site of Nakatsumiya from ancient times, known as the Ōshima Mitake Archaeological Site. * Mt. Mitake – The highest peak on the island, home to Mitake Shrine at its summit. The summit has an observation platform. * Grave of {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|12=draft|12=draft}} – According to tradition, Munetō was exiled here and spent his final days on the island. * Yume-no-Sayoshima – A small island covered by pines on the east side of Ōshima. In the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Renga poet|ja|連歌師|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Iio Sōgi|ja|宗祇|12=draft|12=draft}} visited and composed waka poetry about it. It is accessible only at low tide. * Kansu Beach – A swimming beach near Yume-no-Sayoshima. * Ōshima Exchange Hall (Ōshima Kōryūkan) – A facility introducing the history and culture of Ōshima and Okinoshima. * Okitsumiya Yohaisho – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. A {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|12=draft|12=draft}} for the sacred island of Okinoshima, the location of Okitsumiya. * Windmill Observation Deck – Known as one of the best scenic spots on the island. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|12=draft|12=draft}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|12=draft|12=draft}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|12=draft|12=draft}} legend. File:Umingu Oshima.jpg|Umingu Ōshima File:Street view near Oshima Port on Oshima Island, Munakata, Fukuoka.JPG|Townscape near Ōshima Port File:Grand torii of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Torii of Munakata Taisha Nakatsumiya File:Abe no Muneto tomb.jpg|Grave of Abe no Munetō File:Yumenosayoshima and Kansu Beach.jpg|Yume-no-Sayoshima File:Oshima Culture Center.jpg|Ōshima Exchange Hall File:宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 - panoramio.jpg|Okitsumiya Yohaisho (Munakata Taisha) File:大島灯台 - panoramio.jpg|Ōshima Lighthouse File:Kamizaki Oshima.jpg|Kamizaki === Accommodations === There are a few inns and guesthouses on the island. A campground called Ōshima Campground is located on the island’s western coast. == Festivals == * {{ill|Miare Festival|ja|みあれ祭|12=draft|12=draft}} – The autumn grand festival of Munakata Taisha, marking the beginning of the Tashima Hōjōe (harvest festival). It is the one time of the year when all three goddesses are enshrined together. == Industry == {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|12=draft|12=draft}} is the main industry, but small-scale {{ill|Agriculture|ja|農業|12=draft|12=draft}} also exists, and specialty products include {{ill|Amanatsu|ja|甘夏|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Akamoku|ja|アカモク|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Sea salt|ja|海塩|12=draft|12=draft}}. In addition, {{ill|Japanese Black|ja|黒毛和種|12=draft|12=draft}} cattle are raised on the western side of the island at Ōshima Ranch. == Transportation == === Land Transportation === {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|ja|福岡県道541号大島循環線|12=draft|12=draft}} runs around the central settlement area near the ferry terminal in the southeast and circles the interior of the island, with additional roads leading into the central settlement and coastal areas. Two sightseeing buses operate around the island: the “Granshima-ru” (run by {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|ja|西鉄バス宗像|12=draft|12=draft}}) and the “Miare-gō” (operated by Minato Taxi). In April 2008, Minato Taxi set up an office on the island with two taxis (currently one), usually stationed at the ferry terminal. Bicycle rentals are also available at the ferry terminal and elsewhere. === Maritime Transportation === From the mainland’s Konominato Port in Munakata City to {{ill|Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島港 (福岡県)|lt=Ōshima Port|lt_ja=大島港|12=draft|12=draft}}, it takes 25 minutes on the municipal ferry “{{ill|Munakata Municipal Ferry|ja|宗像市営渡船|lt=Ferry Oshima|lt_ja=フェリーおおしま|12=draft|12=draft}}” or 15 minutes on the passenger boat “Shiokaze.” The schedule and current operating status are posted on Munakata City’s website. There are also private sea taxis. To reach Konominato Port, take the bus bound for Konominato Wharf from {{ill|Tōgō Station|ja|東郷駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (Nishitetsu Bus Munakata); get off at the final stop. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. Slightly south of the ferry terminal is Ōshima Fishing Port, while Miyazaki Fishing Port is to the northeast. Homes and settlements are concentrated around these port areas. The population is 540 with 278 households (from the Reiwa 2 {{ill|National Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本)|lt=National Census|lt_ja=国勢調査|12=draft|12=draft}}). The island has {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|12=draft|12=draft}}, a {{ill|compulsory education school|ja|義務教育学校|12=draft|12=draft}}. == History == In [[1889]] (Meiji 22), under the {{ill|Town and Village Act|ja|町村制|12=draft|12=draft}}, it became {{ill|Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島村 (福岡県)|lt=Oshima Village|lt_ja=大島村|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata District|ja|宗像郡|12=draft|12=draft}}. From May 27 to 28, 1905, the {{ill|Battle of Tsushima|ja|日本海海戦|12=draft|12=draft}} took place offshore, and many Russian soldiers’ bodies washed ashore on Ōshima.[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ Katsuya Kodama “Memorial Service for the Russo-Japanese War on Munakata City’s Ōshima ~A New Bridge of Friendship and Peace between Japan and Russia!~” (November 3, 2013)] (Accessed January 16, 2018) Residents are said to have buried them respectfully. On March 28, 2005, the village was merged into Munakata City. Beginning in 1935 (Shōwa 10), as part of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|12=draft|12=draft}}, a battery was constructed on the island’s northern coast (Ōshima Battery) equipped with four {{ill|Type 45 15 cm Cannon|ja|四五式十五糎加農砲|12=draft|12=draft}}. Associated facilities included an observation post, underground ammunition depot, a mobile 150 cm searchlight, and a power station. After the war, these cannons were removed, but their mounts and other remnants remain. Since 2012, a Japan–Russia joint memorial service has been held for those who died in the Battle of Tsushima, and in November 2013, a monument to the war dead was erected in front of the former Ōshima Battery. In July 2017 ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 29), Nakatsumiya and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho were inscribed as part of the “{{ill|Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|ja|「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|12=draft|12=draft}}” World Heritage Site. == Religious Facilities == At the summit of Mt. Mitake stands an observation platform and the Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) of Nakatsumiya, called {{ill|Mitake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}}. In ancient times, this was a ritual site for Nakatsumiya. Nearby is the Orihime-Hikoboshi Shrine, and local tradition holds that this place is the birthplace of Japan’s Tanabata legend. Near the port is Nakatsumiya of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}}, dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the {{ill|The Three Female Deities of Munakata|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|12=draft|12=draft}}. On the north side of the island is the {{ill|Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|ja|沖津宮遙拝所|lt=Okitsumiya Yohaisho|lt_ja=沖津宮遙拝所|12=draft|12=draft}}, where one can worship the distant island of Okinoshima, home to Okitsumiya, which is forbidden to women. On clear days, one can faintly see Okinoshima from there, but it cannot be seen on cloudy or rainy days. These two sites are part of the “Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region,” a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. Additionally, Ōshima is traditionally said to be the place where {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|12=draft|12=draft}} spent his final years in exile. It is also on the route of the {{ill|Kyushu Olle|ja|九州オルレ|12=draft|12=draft}} hiking course. == Major Facilities and Attractions on the Island == === Main Facilities === * Municipal Office – Munakata City Ōshima Administrative Center * School – {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|12=draft|12=draft}} * Nursery – Ōshima Nursery School === Tourist Attractions === * Umingu Ōshima – A marine experience facility offering {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sea kayaking|ja|シーカヤック|12=draft|12=draft}}. * {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} Nakatsumiya – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. Dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the Munakata Three Sisters. * {{ill|Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|ja|御嶽神社 (宗像市)|lt=Mitake Shrine|lt_ja=御嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}} – The Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) and original sacred site of Nakatsumiya from ancient times, known as the Ōshima Mitake Archaeological Site. * Mt. Mitake – The highest peak on the island, home to Mitake Shrine at its summit. The summit has an observation platform. * Grave of {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|12=draft|12=draft}} – According to tradition, Munetō was exiled here and spent his final days on the island. * Yume-no-Sayoshima – A small island covered by pines on the east side of Ōshima. In the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Renga poet|ja|連歌師|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Iio Sōgi|ja|宗祇|12=draft|12=draft}} visited and composed waka poetry about it. It is accessible only at low tide. * Kansu Beach – A swimming beach near Yume-no-Sayoshima. * Ōshima Exchange Hall (Ōshima Kōryūkan) – A facility introducing the history and culture of Ōshima and Okinoshima. * Okitsumiya Yohaisho – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. A {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|12=draft|12=draft}} for the sacred island of Okinoshima, the location of Okitsumiya. * Windmill Observation Deck – Known as one of the best scenic spots on the island. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|12=draft|12=draft}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|12=draft|12=draft}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|12=draft|12=draft}} legend. File:Umingu Oshima.jpg|Umingu Ōshima File:Street view near Oshima Port on Oshima Island, Munakata, Fukuoka.JPG|Townscape near Ōshima Port File:Grand torii of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Torii of Munakata Taisha Nakatsumiya File:Abe no Muneto tomb.jpg|Grave of Abe no Munetō File:Yumenosayoshima and Kansu Beach.jpg|Yume-no-Sayoshima File:Oshima Culture Center.jpg|Ōshima Exchange Hall File:宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 - panoramio.jpg|Okitsumiya Yohaisho (Munakata Taisha) File:大島灯台 - panoramio.jpg|Ōshima Lighthouse File:Kamizaki Oshima.jpg|Kamizaki === Accommodations === There are a few inns and guesthouses on the island. A campground called Ōshima Campground is located on the island’s western coast. == Festivals == * {{ill|Miare Festival|ja|みあれ祭|12=draft|12=draft}} – The autumn grand festival of Munakata Taisha, marking the beginning of the Tashima Hōjōe (harvest festival). It is the one time of the year when all three goddesses are enshrined together. == Industry == {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|12=draft|12=draft}} is the main industry, but small-scale {{ill|Agriculture|ja|農業|12=draft|12=draft}} also exists, and specialty products include {{ill|Amanatsu|ja|甘夏|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Akamoku|ja|アカモク|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Sea salt|ja|海塩|12=draft|12=draft}}. In addition, {{ill|Japanese Black|ja|黒毛和種|12=draft|12=draft}} cattle are raised on the western side of the island at Ōshima Ranch. == Transportation == === Land Transportation === {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|ja|福岡県道541号大島循環線|12=draft|12=draft}} runs around the central settlement area near the ferry terminal in the southeast and circles the interior of the island, with additional roads leading into the central settlement and coastal areas. Two sightseeing buses operate around the island: the “Granshima-ru” (run by {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|ja|西鉄バス宗像|12=draft|12=draft}}) and the “Miare-gō” (operated by Minato Taxi). In April 2008, Minato Taxi set up an office on the island with two taxis (currently one), usually stationed at the ferry terminal. Bicycle rentals are also available at the ferry terminal and elsewhere. === Maritime Transportation === From the mainland’s Konominato Port in Munakata City to {{ill|Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島港 (福岡県)|lt=Ōshima Port|lt_ja=大島港|12=draft|12=draft}}, it takes 25 minutes on the municipal ferry “{{ill|Munakata Municipal Ferry|ja|宗像市営渡船|lt=Ferry Oshima|lt_ja=フェリーおおしま|12=draft|12=draft}}” or 15 minutes on the passenger boat “Shiokaze.” The schedule and current operating status are posted on Munakata City’s website. There are also private sea taxis. To reach Konominato Port, take the bus bound for Konominato Wharf from {{ill|Tōgō Station|ja|東郷駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (Nishitetsu Bus Munakata); get off at the final stop. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. {{Location map|Japan |float=right |width=300 | caption = Location of Ō Shima in Japan. | label = Ō Shima|position=right|background=white|lat=33.90222|long=130.42414}} '''Ōshima''' (大島) is an {{ill|Island|ja|島|12=draft|12=draft}} (an inhabited island) in {{ill|Munakata City|ja|宗像市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft|12=draft}}, facing the boundary between {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Genkai-nada|ja|玄界灘|12=draft|12=draft}}. As part of the Chikuzen Islands area, it is designated as a Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Area under the {{ill|Remote Islands Development Act|ja|離島振興法|12=draft|12=draft}}.[https://www.mlit.go.jp/kokudoseisaku/chirit/content/001619210.pdf Fukuoka Prefecture "Fukuoka Prefecture Remote Islands Development Plan (FY2023 – FY2032)"] – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (Accessed September 23, 2024) The island’s area is about 7.17 {{ill|square kilometers|ja|平方キロメートル|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is also known as Chikuzen-Ōshima and is one of the {{ill|the Seven Inlets of Munakata|ja|宗像七浦|12=draft|12=draft}}, home to the Middle Shrine (Nakatsumiya) of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho, which are part of a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its catchphrase is “Island that Protects the Gods.” == Overview == {{Created by bot|Lsjbot|Japan|date=2017-02}} :''For other places with the same name, see [[Ō Shima]].'' {{geobox | 1 = Island | name = Ō Shima | native_name = 大島 | other_name = Ō Sima | category = Island | etymology = | nickname = | image = | image_caption = | country = {{flag|Japan}} | country_flag = true | state = [[Fukuoka Prefecture]] | state_type = Prefecture | region = | region_type = | district = | district_type = | municipality = | municipality_type = | parent = | range = | range_type = Archipelago | border = | part = | city = | capital = | landmark = | river = | location = | lat_d = 33.90222 | lat_m = | lat_s = | lat_NS = | long_d = 130.42414 | long_m = | long_s = | long_EW = | highest = | highest_location = | highest_region = | highest_country = | highest_elevation = | highest_lat_d = | highest_lat_m = | highest_lat_s = | highest_lat_NS = | highest_long_d = | highest_long_m = | highest_long_s = | highest_long_EW = | length = | length_orientation = | width = | width_orientation = | height = | area = 7.46 | population = | population_date = | population_note = | population_density = | population_density_note = | public = | access = | timezone = [[Japan Standard Time|JST]] | utc_offset = +9 | timezone_DST = | utc_offset_DST = | postal_code = | area_code = | code = | free = | free_type = | map = | map_caption = | map_locator_x = | map_locator_y = | footnotes = | other_name1 = Ō-shima | other_name2 = 筑前大島 | other_name3 = Tchikuzen-Ōshima | elevation = 128 | timezone_label = Asia/Tokyo | geonames = 1853774 }} [[Island]] '''Ō Shima''' ([[Japanese]]: '''大島''', '''筑前大島''') is in [[Japan]]. It is located in the prefecture of [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], in the southwestern part of the country, about {{formatnum:900}} km west of [[Tokyo (the capital city of Japan)|Tokyo]], the capital of the country. It covers an area of approximately {{formatnum:7.5}} square kilometers. The terrain of Ō Shima is flat.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The highest point of the island is {{formatnum:206}} meters above sea level. It spans 3.1 km from north to south and 4.0 km from east to west.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The climate is [[temperate]]. The average temperature is {{formatnum:15}} [[°C]]. The warmest month is August, at {{formatnum:24}} [[°C]], and the coldest is February, at {{formatnum:6}} °C. The average annual rainfall is {{formatnum:2130}} millimeters. The wettest month is July, with {{formatnum:410}} millimeters of rain, and the driest is {{citation needed|Oshima (Fukuoka)}}January, with {{formatnum:47}} millimeters. {| class="climate chart" |- | '''Ō Shima Climate Data''' | {{citation needed|Oshima (Fukuoka)}}January | 5 | 8 | 47 | February | 4 | 7 | 157| March | 6 | 13 | 136| April | 10 | 17 | 120| May | 14 | 20 | 89| June | 15 | 21 | 294| July | 20 | 22 | 410| August | 23 | 26 | 383| September | 19 | 21 | 146| October | 17 | 21 | 126| November | 12 | 16 | 124| December | 7 | 11 | 98|- | colspan="13" | Data source: |} == Geography == [[File:Oshima_Island,_Munakata_Fukuoka_Aerial_photograph.2010.jpg|alt=Ōshima aerial photograph.|thumb|280x280px]]
Created by combining 26 images taken on June 3, 2010. {{ill|GSI Aerial Photograph|ja|国土航空写真|12=draft|12=draft}}. Ōshima is located about 6.5 {{ill|kilometers|ja|キロメートル|12=draft|12=draft}} northwest of the Konominato Port on the Munakata mainland. About 5 km to the east lies {{ill|Jinoshima|ja|地島|12=draft|12=draft}}. Together with Jinoshima and {{ill|Okinoshima|ja|沖ノ島|12=draft|12=draft}}, it marks the boundary between {{ill|Genkai Sea|ja|玄界灘|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|12=draft|12=draft}}—the sea on the west side of the island is Genkai-nada, and on the east side is Hibiki-nada. Its total area is 7.17 km{{sup|2}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001015648.pdf List of Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Areas]}} – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, National and Regional Policy Bureau, Remote Islands Development Division, making it the largest of the remote islands in Fukuoka Prefecture. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|12=draft|12=draft}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|12=draft|12=draft}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|12=draft|12=draft}} legend. A campground called Ōshima Campground is located on the island’s western coast. == Festivals == * {{ill|Miare Festival|ja|みあれ祭|12=draft|12=draft}} – The autumn grand festival of Munakata Taisha, marking the beginning of the Tashima Hōjōe (harvest festival). It is the one time of the year when all three goddesses are enshrined together. == Industry == {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|12=draft|12=draft}} is the main industry, but small-scale {{ill|Agriculture|ja|農業|12=draft|12=draft}} also exists, and specialty products include {{ill|Amanatsu|ja|甘夏|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Akamoku|ja|アカモク|12=draft|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Sea salt|ja|海塩|12=draft|12=draft}}. In addition, {{ill|Japanese Black|ja|黒毛和種|12=draft|12=draft}} cattle are raised on the western side of the island at Ōshima Ranch. == Transportation == === Land Transportation === {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|ja|福岡県道541号大島循環線|12=draft|12=draft}} runs around the central settlement area near the ferry terminal in the southeast and circles the interior of the island, with additional roads leading into the central settlement and coastal areas. Two sightseeing buses operate around the island: the “Granshima-ru” (run by {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|ja|西鉄バス宗像|12=draft|12=draft}}) and the “Miare-gō” (operated by Minato Taxi). In April 2008, Minato Taxi set up an office on the island with two taxis (currently one), usually stationed at the ferry terminal. Bicycle rentals are also available at the ferry terminal and elsewhere. === Maritime Transportation === From the mainland’s Konominato Port in Munakata City to {{ill|Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島港 (福岡県)|lt=Ōshima Port|lt_ja=大島港|12=draft|12=draft}}, it takes 25 minutes on the municipal ferry “{{ill|Munakata Municipal Ferry|ja|宗像市営渡船|lt=Ferry Oshima|lt_ja=フェリーおおしま|12=draft|12=draft}}” or 15 minutes on the passenger boat “Shiokaze.” The schedule and current operating status are posted on Munakata City’s website. There are also private sea taxis. To reach Konominato Port, take the bus bound for Konominato Wharf from {{ill|Tōgō Station|ja|東郷駅|12=draft|12=draft}} (Nishitetsu Bus Munakata); get off at the final stop. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. {{Location map|Japan |float=right |width=300 | caption = Location of Ō Shima in Japan. | label = Ō Shima|position=right|background=white|lat=33.90222|long=130.42414}} '''Ōshima''' (大島) is an {{ill|Island|ja|島|12=draft|12=draft}} (an inhabited island) in {{ill|Munakata City|ja|宗像市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|12=draft|12=draft}}, facing the boundary between {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Genkai-nada|ja|玄界灘|12=draft|12=draft}}. As part of the Chikuzen Islands area, it is designated as a Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Area under the {{ill|Remote Islands Development Act|ja|離島振興法|12=draft|12=draft}}.[https://www.mlit.go.jp/kokudoseisaku/chirit/content/001619210.pdf Fukuoka Prefecture "Fukuoka Prefecture Remote Islands Development Plan (FY2023 – FY2032)"] – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (Accessed September 23, 2024) The island’s area is about 7.17 {{ill|square kilometers|ja|平方キロメートル|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is also known as Chikuzen-Ōshima and is one of the {{ill|the Seven Inlets of Munakata|ja|宗像七浦|12=draft|12=draft}}, home to the Middle Shrine (Nakatsumiya) of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho, which are part of a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its catchphrase is “Island that Protects the Gods.” == Overview == {{Created by bot|Lsjbot|Japan|date=2017-02}} :''For other places with the same name, see [[Ō Shima]].'' {{geobox | 1 = Island | name = Ō Shima | native_name = 大島 | other_name = Ō Sima | category = Island | etymology = | nickname = | image = | image_caption = | country = {{flag|Japan}} | country_flag = true | state = [[Fukuoka Prefecture]] | state_type = Prefecture | region = | region_type = | district = | district_type = | municipality = | municipality_type = | parent = | range = | range_type = Archipelago | border = | part = | city = | capital = | landmark = | river = | location = | lat_d = 33.90222 | lat_m = | lat_s = | lat_NS = | long_d = 130.42414 | long_m = | long_s = | long_EW = | highest = | highest_location = | highest_region = | highest_country = | highest_elevation = | highest_lat_d = | highest_lat_m = | highest_lat_s = | highest_lat_NS = | highest_long_d = | highest_long_m = | highest_long_s = | highest_long_EW = | length = | length_orientation = | width = | width_orientation = | height = | area = 7.46 | population = | population_date = | population_note = | population_density = | population_density_note = | public = | access = | timezone = [[Japan Standard Time|JST]] | utc_offset = +9 | timezone_DST = | utc_offset_DST = | postal_code = | area_code = | code = | free = | free_type = | map = | map_caption = | map_locator_x = | map_locator_y = | footnotes = | other_name1 = Ō-shima | other_name2 = 筑前大島 | other_name3 = Tchikuzen-Ōshima | elevation = 128 | timezone_label = Asia/Tokyo | geonames = 1853774 }} [[Island]] '''Ō Shima''' ([[Japanese]]: '''大島''', '''筑前大島''') is in [[Japan]]. It is located in the prefecture of [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], in the southwestern part of the country, about {{formatnum:900}} km west of [[Tokyo (the capital city of Japan)|Tokyo]], the capital of the country. It covers an area of approximately {{formatnum:7.5}} square kilometers. The terrain of Ō Shima is flat.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The highest point of the island is {{formatnum:206}} meters above sea level. It spans 3.1 km from north to south and 4.0 km from east to west.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The climate is [[temperate]]. The average temperature is {{formatnum:15}} [[°C]]. The warmest month is August, at {{formatnum:24}} [[°C]], and the coldest is February, at {{formatnum:6}} °C. The average annual rainfall is {{formatnum:2130}} millimeters. The wettest month is July, with {{formatnum:410}} millimeters of rain, and the driest is {{citation needed|Oshima (Fukuoka)}}January, with {{formatnum:47}} millimeters. {| class="climate chart" |- | '''Ō Shima Climate Data''' | {{citation needed|Oshima (Fukuoka)}}January | 5 | 8 | 47 | February | 4 | 7 | 157| March | 6 | 13 | 136| April | 10 | 17 | 120| May | 14 | 20 | 89| June | 15 | 21 | 294| July | 20 | 22 | 410| August | 23 | 26 | 383| September | 19 | 21 | 146| October | 17 | 21 | 126| November | 12 | 16 | 124| December | 7 | 11 | 98|- | colspan="13" | Data source: |} == Geography == [[File:Oshima_Island,_Munakata_Fukuoka_Aerial_photograph.2010.jpg|alt=Ōshima aerial photograph.|thumb|280x280px]]
Created by combining 26 images taken on June 3, 2010. {{ill|GSI Aerial Photograph|ja|国土航空写真|12=draft|12=draft}}. Ōshima is located about 6.5 {{ill|kilometers|ja|キロメートル|12=draft|12=draft}} northwest of the Konominato Port on the Munakata mainland. About 5 km to the east lies {{ill|Jinoshima|ja|地島|12=draft|12=draft}}. Together with Jinoshima and {{ill|Okinoshima|ja|沖ノ島|12=draft|12=draft}}, it marks the boundary between {{ill|Genkai Sea|ja|玄界灘|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|12=draft|12=draft}}—the sea on the west side of the island is Genkai-nada, and on the east side is Hibiki-nada. Its total area is 7.17 km{{sup|2}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001015648.pdf List of Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Areas]}} – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, National and Regional Policy Bureau, Remote Islands Development Division, making it the largest of the remote islands in Fukuoka Prefecture. Much of the island is hilly with steep terrain, and the highest peak is Mitake (224 m) in the island’s center. On the eastern side of the island is Ōshima Port, where ferries connect to the mainland, and a ferry terminal is located there. Slightly south of the ferry terminal is Ōshima Fishing Port, while Miyazaki Fishing Port is to the northeast. Homes and settlements are concentrated around these port areas. The population is 540 with 278 households (from the Reiwa 2 {{ill|National Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本)|lt=National Census|lt_ja=国勢調査|12=draft|12=draft}}). The island has {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|12=draft|12=draft}}, a {{ill|compulsory education school|ja|義務教育学校|12=draft|12=draft}}. == History == In [[1889]] (Meiji 22), under the {{ill|Town and Village Act|ja|町村制|12=draft|12=draft}}, it became {{ill|Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島村 (福岡県)|lt=Oshima Village|lt_ja=大島村|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata District|ja|宗像郡|12=draft|12=draft}}. From May 27 to 28, 1905, the {{ill|Battle of Tsushima|ja|日本海海戦|12=draft|12=draft}} took place offshore, and many Russian soldiers’ bodies washed ashore on Ōshima.[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ Katsuya Kodama “Memorial Service for the Russo-Japanese War on Munakata City’s Ōshima ~A New Bridge of Friendship and Peace between Japan and Russia!~” (November 3, 2013)] (Accessed January 16, 2018) Residents are said to have buried them respectfully. On March 28, 2005, the village was merged into Munakata City. Beginning in 1935 (Shōwa 10), as part of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|12=draft|12=draft}}, a battery was constructed on the island’s northern coast (Ōshima Battery) equipped with four {{ill|Type 45 15 cm Cannon|ja|四五式十五糎加農砲|12=draft|12=draft}}. Associated facilities included an observation post, underground ammunition depot, a mobile 150 cm searchlight, and a power station. After the war, these cannons were removed, but their mounts and other remnants remain. Since 2012, a Japan–Russia joint memorial service has been held for those who died in the Battle of Tsushima, and in November 2013, a monument to the war dead was erected in front of the former Ōshima Battery. In July 2017 ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|12=draft|12=draft}} 29), Nakatsumiya and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho were inscribed as part of the “{{ill|Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|ja|「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|12=draft|12=draft}}” World Heritage Site. == Religious Facilities == At the summit of Mt. Mitake stands an observation platform and the Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) of Nakatsumiya, called {{ill|Mitake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}}. In ancient times, this was a ritual site for Nakatsumiya. Nearby is the Orihime-Hikoboshi Shrine, and local tradition holds that this place is the birthplace of Japan’s Tanabata legend. Near the port is Nakatsumiya of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}}, dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the {{ill|The Three Female Deities of Munakata|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|12=draft|12=draft}}. On the north side of the island is the {{ill|Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|ja|沖津宮遙拝所|lt=Okitsumiya Yohaisho|lt_ja=沖津宮遙拝所|12=draft|12=draft}}, where one can worship the distant island of Okinoshima, home to Okitsumiya, which is forbidden to women. On clear days, one can faintly see Okinoshima from there, but it cannot be seen on cloudy or rainy days. These two sites are part of the “Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region,” a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|12=draft|12=draft}}. Additionally, Ōshima is traditionally said to be the place where {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|12=draft|12=draft}} spent his final years in exile. It is also on the route of the {{ill|Kyushu Olle|ja|九州オルレ|12=draft|12=draft}} hiking course. == Major Facilities and Attractions on the Island == === Main Facilities === * Municipal Office – Munakata City Ōshima Administrative Center * School – {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|12=draft|12=draft}} * Nursery – Ōshima Nursery School === Tourist Attractions === * Umingu Ōshima – A marine experience facility offering {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sea kayaking|ja|シーカヤック|12=draft|12=draft}}. * {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|12=draft|12=draft}} Nakatsumiya – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. Dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the Munakata Three Sisters. * {{ill|Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|ja|御嶽神社 (宗像市)|lt=Mitake Shrine|lt_ja=御嶽神社|12=draft|12=draft}} – The Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) and original sacred site of Nakatsumiya from ancient times, known as the Ōshima Mitake Archaeological Site. * Mt. Mitake – The highest peak on the island, home to Mitake Shrine at its summit. The summit has an observation platform. * Grave of {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|12=draft|12=draft}} – According to tradition, Munetō was exiled here and spent his final days on the island. * Yume-no-Sayoshima – A small island covered by pines on the east side of Ōshima. In the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Renga poet|ja|連歌師|12=draft|12=draft}} {{ill|Iio Sōgi|ja|宗祇|12=draft|12=draft}} visited and composed waka poetry about it. It is accessible only at low tide. * Kansu Beach – A swimming beach near Yume-no-Sayoshima. * Ōshima Exchange Hall (Ōshima Kōryūkan) – A facility introducing the history and culture of Ōshima and Okinoshima. * Okitsumiya Yohaisho – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. A {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|12=draft|12=draft}} for the sacred island of Okinoshima, the location of Okitsumiya. * Windmill Observation Deck – Known as one of the best scenic spots on the island. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|12=draft|12=draft}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|12=draft|12=draft}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|12=draft|12=draft}} legend. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|12=draft|12=draft}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|12=draft|12=draft}}. {{Location map|Japan |float=right |width=300 | caption = Location of Ō Shima in Japan. | label = Ō Shima|position=right|background=white|lat=33.90222|long=130.42414}} '''Ōshima''' (大島) is an {{ill|Island|ja|島|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (an inhabited island) in {{ill|Munakata City|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, facing the boundary between {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Genkai-nada|ja|玄界灘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. As part of the Chikuzen Islands area, it is designated as a Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Area under the {{ill|Remote Islands Development Act|ja|離島振興法|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.[https://www.mlit.go.jp/kokudoseisaku/chirit/content/001619210.pdf Fukuoka Prefecture "Fukuoka Prefecture Remote Islands Development Plan (FY2023 – FY2032)"] – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (Accessed September 23, 2024) The island’s area is about 7.17 {{ill|square kilometers|ja|平方キロメートル|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. It is also known as Chikuzen-Ōshima and is one of the {{ill|the Seven Inlets of Munakata|ja|宗像七浦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, home to the Middle Shrine (Nakatsumiya) of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho, which are part of a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Its catchphrase is “Island that Protects the Gods.” == Overview == {{Created by bot|Lsjbot|Japan|date=2017-02}} :''For other places with the same name, see [[Ō Shima]].'' {{geobox | 1 = Island | name = Ō Shima | native_name = 大島 | other_name = Ō Sima | category = Island | etymology = | nickname = | image = | image_caption = | country = {{flag|Japan}} | country_flag = true | state = [[Fukuoka Prefecture]] | state_type = Prefecture | region = | region_type = | district = | district_type = | municipality = | municipality_type = | parent = | range = | range_type = Archipelago | border = | part = | city = | capital = | landmark = | river = | location = | lat_d = 33.90222 | lat_m = | lat_s = | lat_NS = | long_d = 130.42414 | long_m = | long_s = | long_EW = | highest = | highest_location = | highest_region = | highest_country = | highest_elevation = | highest_lat_d = | highest_lat_m = | highest_lat_s = | highest_lat_NS = | highest_long_d = | highest_long_m = | highest_long_s = | highest_long_EW = | length = | length_orientation = | width = | width_orientation = | height = | area = 7.46 | population = | population_date = | population_note = | population_density = | population_density_note = | public = | access = | timezone = [[Japan Standard Time|JST]] | utc_offset = +9 | timezone_DST = | utc_offset_DST = | postal_code = | area_code = | code = | free = | free_type = | map = | map_caption = | map_locator_x = | map_locator_y = | footnotes = | other_name1 = Ō-shima | other_name2 = 筑前大島 | other_name3 = Tchikuzen-Ōshima | elevation = 128 | timezone_label = Asia/Tokyo | geonames = 1853774 }} [[Island]] '''Ō Shima''' ([[Japanese]]: '''大島''', '''筑前大島''') is in [[Japan]]. It is located in the prefecture of [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], in the southwestern part of the country, about {{formatnum:900}} km west of [[Tokyo (the capital city of Japan)|Tokyo]], the capital of the country. It covers an area of approximately {{formatnum:7.5}} square kilometers. The terrain of Ō Shima is flat.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The highest point of the island is {{formatnum:206}} meters above sea level. It spans 3.1 km from north to south and 4.0 km from east to west.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The climate is [[temperate]]. The average temperature is {{formatnum:15}} [[°C]]. The warmest month is August, at {{formatnum:24}} [[°C]], and the coldest is February, at {{formatnum:6}} °C. The average annual rainfall is {{formatnum:2130}} millimeters. The wettest month is July, with {{formatnum:410}} millimeters of rain, and the driest is {{citation needed|Oshima (Fukuoka)}}January, with {{formatnum:47}} millimeters. {| class="climate chart" |- | '''Ō Shima Climate Data''' | {{citation needed|Oshima (Fukuoka)}}January | 5 | 8 | 47 | February | 4 | 7 | 157| March | 6 | 13 | 136| April | 10 | 17 | 120| May | 14 | 20 | 89| June | 15 | 21 | 294| July | 20 | 22 | 410| August | 23 | 26 | 383| September | 19 | 21 | 146| October | 17 | 21 | 126| November | 12 | 16 | 124| December | 7 | 11 | 98|- | colspan="13" | Data source: |} == Geography == [[File:Oshima_Island,_Munakata_Fukuoka_Aerial_photograph.2010.jpg|alt=Ōshima aerial photograph.|thumb|280x280px]]
Created by combining 26 images taken on June 3, 2010. {{ill|GSI Aerial Photograph|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Ōshima is located about 6.5 {{ill|kilometers|ja|キロメートル|qq=draft|qq=draft}} northwest of the Konominato Port on the Munakata mainland. About 5 km to the east lies {{ill|Jinoshima|ja|地島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Together with Jinoshima and {{ill|Okinoshima|ja|沖ノ島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it marks the boundary between {{ill|Genkai Sea|ja|玄界灘|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}—the sea on the west side of the island is Genkai-nada, and on the east side is Hibiki-nada. Its total area is 7.17 km{{sup|2}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001015648.pdf List of Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Areas]}} – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, National and Regional Policy Bureau, Remote Islands Development Division, making it the largest of the remote islands in Fukuoka Prefecture. Much of the island is hilly with steep terrain, and the highest peak is Mitake (224 m) in the island’s center. On the eastern side of the island is Ōshima Port, where ferries connect to the mainland, and a ferry terminal is located there. Slightly south of the ferry terminal is Ōshima Fishing Port, while Miyazaki Fishing Port is to the northeast. Homes and settlements are concentrated around these port areas. The population is 540 with 278 households (from the Reiwa 2 {{ill|National Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本)|lt=National Census|lt_ja=国勢調査|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). The island has {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a {{ill|compulsory education school|ja|義務教育学校|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == In [[1889]] (Meiji 22), under the {{ill|Town and Village Act|ja|町村制|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it became {{ill|Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島村 (福岡県)|lt=Oshima Village|lt_ja=大島村|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata District|ja|宗像郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. From May 27 to 28, 1905, the {{ill|Battle of Tsushima|ja|日本海海戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took place offshore, and many Russian soldiers’ bodies washed ashore on Ōshima.[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ Katsuya Kodama “Memorial Service for the Russo-Japanese War on Munakata City’s Ōshima ~A New Bridge of Friendship and Peace between Japan and Russia!~” (November 3, 2013)] (Accessed January 16, 2018) Residents are said to have buried them respectfully. On March 28, 2005, the village was merged into Munakata City. Beginning in 1935 (Shōwa 10), as part of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a battery was constructed on the island’s northern coast (Ōshima Battery) equipped with four {{ill|Type 45 15 cm Cannon|ja|四五式十五糎加農砲|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Associated facilities included an observation post, underground ammunition depot, a mobile 150 cm searchlight, and a power station. After the war, these cannons were removed, but their mounts and other remnants remain. Since 2012, a Japan–Russia joint memorial service has been held for those who died in the Battle of Tsushima, and in November 2013, a monument to the war dead was erected in front of the former Ōshima Battery. In July 2017 ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 29), Nakatsumiya and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho were inscribed as part of the “{{ill|Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|ja|「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” World Heritage Site. == Religious Facilities == At the summit of Mt. Mitake stands an observation platform and the Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) of Nakatsumiya, called {{ill|Mitake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In ancient times, this was a ritual site for Nakatsumiya. Nearby is the Orihime-Hikoboshi Shrine, and local tradition holds that this place is the birthplace of Japan’s Tanabata legend. Near the port is Nakatsumiya of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the {{ill|The Three Female Deities of Munakata|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On the north side of the island is the {{ill|Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|ja|沖津宮遙拝所|lt=Okitsumiya Yohaisho|lt_ja=沖津宮遙拝所|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, where one can worship the distant island of Okinoshima, home to Okitsumiya, which is forbidden to women. On clear days, one can faintly see Okinoshima from there, but it cannot be seen on cloudy or rainy days. These two sites are part of the “Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region,” a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Additionally, Ōshima is traditionally said to be the place where {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft}} spent his final years in exile. It is also on the route of the {{ill|Kyushu Olle|ja|九州オルレ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} hiking course. == Major Facilities and Attractions on the Island == === Main Facilities === * Municipal Office – Munakata City Ōshima Administrative Center * School – {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * Nursery – Ōshima Nursery School === Tourist Attractions === * Umingu Ōshima – A marine experience facility offering {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sea kayaking|ja|シーカヤック|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Nakatsumiya – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. Dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the Munakata Three Sisters. * {{ill|Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|ja|御嶽神社 (宗像市)|lt=Mitake Shrine|lt_ja=御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – The Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) and original sacred site of Nakatsumiya from ancient times, known as the Ōshima Mitake Archaeological Site. * Mt. Mitake – The highest peak on the island, home to Mitake Shrine at its summit. The summit has an observation platform. * Grave of {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – According to tradition, Munetō was exiled here and spent his final days on the island. * Yume-no-Sayoshima – A small island covered by pines on the east side of Ōshima. In the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Renga poet|ja|連歌師|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Iio Sōgi|ja|宗祇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} visited and composed waka poetry about it. It is accessible only at low tide. * Kansu Beach – A swimming beach near Yume-no-Sayoshima. * Ōshima Exchange Hall (Ōshima Kōryūkan) – A facility introducing the history and culture of Ōshima and Okinoshima. * Okitsumiya Yohaisho – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. A {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|qq=draft|qq=draft}} for the sacred island of Okinoshima, the location of Okitsumiya. * Windmill Observation Deck – Known as one of the best scenic spots on the island. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|qq=draft|qq=draft}} legend. File:Umingu Oshima.jpg|Umingu Ōshima File:Street view near Oshima Port on Oshima Island, Munakata, Fukuoka.JPG|Townscape near Ōshima Port File:Grand torii of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Torii of Munakata Taisha Nakatsumiya File:Abe no Muneto tomb.jpg|Grave of Abe no Munetō File:Yumenosayoshima and Kansu Beach.jpg|Yume-no-Sayoshima File:Oshima Culture Center.jpg|Ōshima Exchange Hall File:宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 - panoramio.jpg|Okitsumiya Yohaisho (Munakata Taisha) File:大島灯台 - panoramio.jpg|Ōshima Lighthouse File:Kamizaki Oshima.jpg|Kamizaki === Accommodations === There are a few inns and guesthouses on the island. A campground called Ōshima Campground is located on the island’s western coast. == Festivals == * {{ill|Miare Festival|ja|みあれ祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – The autumn grand festival of Munakata Taisha, marking the beginning of the Tashima Hōjōe (harvest festival). It is the one time of the year when all three goddesses are enshrined together. == Industry == {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is the main industry, but small-scale {{ill|Agriculture|ja|農業|qq=draft|qq=draft}} also exists, and specialty products include {{ill|Amanatsu|ja|甘夏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Akamoku|ja|アカモク|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Sea salt|ja|海塩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In addition, {{ill|Japanese Black|ja|黒毛和種|qq=draft|qq=draft}} cattle are raised on the western side of the island at Ōshima Ranch. == Transportation == === Land Transportation === {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|ja|福岡県道541号大島循環線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} runs around the central settlement area near the ferry terminal in the southeast and circles the interior of the island, with additional roads leading into the central settlement and coastal areas. Two sightseeing buses operate around the island: the “Granshima-ru” (run by {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|ja|西鉄バス宗像|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and the “Miare-gō” (operated by Minato Taxi). In April 2008, Minato Taxi set up an office on the island with two taxis (currently one), usually stationed at the ferry terminal. Bicycle rentals are also available at the ferry terminal and elsewhere. === Maritime Transportation === From the mainland’s Konominato Port in Munakata City to {{ill|Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島港 (福岡県)|lt=Ōshima Port|lt_ja=大島港|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it takes 25 minutes on the municipal ferry “{{ill|Munakata Municipal Ferry|ja|宗像市営渡船|lt=Ferry Oshima|lt_ja=フェリーおおしま|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” or 15 minutes on the passenger boat “Shiokaze.” The schedule and current operating status are posted on Munakata City’s website. There are also private sea taxis. To reach Konominato Port, take the bus bound for Konominato Wharf from {{ill|Tōgō Station|ja|東郷駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Nishitetsu Bus Munakata); get off at the final stop. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. File:Oosimakou.jpg|Ōshima Port Ferry Terminal (2009) File:Munakata City Ferry Oshima.jpg|Ferry Oshima (2018) == References == == See Also == * {{ill|Geography of Japan|ja|日本の地理|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|List of islands of Japan|ja|日本の島の一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Ōshima, Munakata}} * [https://maps.gsi.go.jp/#14/33.897741/130.433164/&base=std&ls=std&disp=1&vs=c1j0h0k0l0u0t0z0r0s0m0f1 GSI Maps] {{ill|Designated Islands of Japan|ja|日本の指定離島|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Normdaten}} {{citation needed|Oshima (Fukuoka)}}[[ceb:Ō_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Fukuoka-ken)]]== References == [{{Geonameslink|gnid=1853774|name=o%20shima}} Ō Shima] at [{{Geonamesabout}} Geonames.org (cc-by)]; {{Infobox 島 | 島名=大島 | 画像= [[File:View of Katsushima Island and Oshima Island from Ferry "Oshima" 2.JPG|250px]] | 画像説明=「[[宗像市営渡船|フェリーおおしま]]」から眺める大島（中央奥）。
手前左側は勝島 | 座標 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|33|54|8.1|N|130|25|32|E|region:JP-40}} | 面積= 7.45 | 周囲= 16.5 | 標高= 224 | 最高峰= | 最大都市= | 諸島= | 海域= [[日本海]]（[[響灘]]） | 国= {{JPN}}（[[福岡県]][[宗像市]]） |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Fukuoka Prefecture#Japan|relief=1|float=center|label=大島}} |OSMズーム = 11 }} '''大島'''（おおしま）は、[[響灘]]と[[玄界灘]]の境界部に面する[[福岡県]][[宗像市]]の[[島]]（有人島）。筑前諸島地域として[[離島振興法]]の離島振興対策実施地域となっている[https://www.mlit.go.jp/kokudoseisaku/chirit/content/001619210.pdf 福岡県「福岡県離島振興計画 （令和5年度 - 令和14年度）」] - 国土交通省（2024年9月23日閲覧）。島の面積は約7.17[[平方キロメートル|km{{sup|2}}]]である。'''筑前大島'''ともいい、[[宗像七浦]]の一つで、[[世界遺産]]の[[宗像大社]]中津宮、沖津宮遙拝所がある。キャッチフレーズは「神守る島」。 == 地理 == [[File:Oshima Island, Munakata Fukuoka Aerial photograph.2010.jpg|thumb|280px|大島の空中写真。
2010年6月3日撮影の26枚を合成作成。{{国土航空写真}}。]] 宗像市本土側の神湊港から北西に約6.5[[キロメートル|km]]の場所に位置する。約5km東の海上には[[地島]]がある。地島・[[沖ノ島]]とともに[[玄界灘]]と[[響灘]]を分ける島で、島の西側の海が玄界灘、東側の海が響灘である。面積7.17[[平方キロメートル|km{{sup|2}}]]で{{PDFlink|[http://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001015648.pdf 離島振興対策実施地域一覧]}} - 国土交通省国土政策局離島振興課、福岡県の離島の中では面積が最大。島の多くは丘陵地であり起伏が激しい。中央部にある御嶽（みたけ：標高224m）は島の最高峰。島の東側には本土との間を結ぶ船が発着する大島港がありフェリーターミナルが置かれる。フェリーターミナルのやや南側に大島漁港、北東側に宮崎漁港がある。人家・集落はこれらの港の周辺部に集中している。人口は540人、世帯数は278世帯（令和2年[[国勢調査 (日本)|国勢調査]]）。島内に[[宗像市立大島学園]]がある（[[義務教育学校]]）。 == 歴史 == [[1889年]]（明治22年）の[[町村制]]施行時に[[宗像郡]][[大島村 (福岡県)|大島村]]として村制を施行。1905年5月27-28日にかけて沖合で[[日本海海戦]]があり、大島にも多くのロシア兵の遺体が流れ着いたが[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ 児玉克哉『宗像市大島で日露戦争の慰霊祭～日本とロシアの新たな友好と平和の懸け橋を！』2013/11/3(日) 15:35　] 2018年1月16日閲覧、住民らはそれを丁寧に埋葬したとされる。[[2005年]][[3月28日]]に宗像市に編入合併された。1935年 (昭和10年)より[[下関要塞]]大島砲台として、島内の北岸に[[四五式十五糎加農砲]]が4門が設置された。周辺に観測所、地下弾薬庫、可搬式150cm射光機、発電所などの付随施設も作られた。戦後カノン砲は撤去されたが、台座などの遺構が残されている。2012年より日本海海戦の戦没者を慰霊する日ロの共同慰霊祭が開催されるようになり、2013年11月に下関要塞大島砲台手前に「日本海海戦・戦死者慰霊碑」が建立された。[[2017年]]（[[平成]]29年）7月には中津宮と沖津宮遙拝所が「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群の一部として世界遺産に登録された。 == 宗教施設 == 御嶽山頂には展望台と中津宮の奥宮にあたる『[[御嶽神社]]』がある。古代は中津宮の祭祀場であった。近くには織姫彦星の社があり、地元では日本の七夕伝説発祥の地とされる。港近くには、[[宗像三女神]]の次女、[[多岐津姫命]]を祀る[[宗像大社]]『'''中津宮'''』がある。北側には[[沖ノ島]]の沖津宮を拝する『'''沖津宮遙拝所'''』がある。女人禁制である沖ノ島を拝するために江戸時代後期に建立された。曇りや雨の日は見えないが晴れた日には遠く微かに島を拝める。この2か所は、'''[[「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群]]'''の構成資産として、[[世界遺産]]に登録されている。また、大島は[[安倍宗任]]が晩年を過ごし没した地とされる伝承の地でもある。九州オルレのコースともなっている。 == 島内の主要施設と名所 == === 主要施設 === * 役場 - 宗像市大島行政センター * 学校 - [[宗像市立大島学園]] * 保育所 - 大島保育所 === 観光名所 === * うみんぐ大島 - [[釣り]]や[[シーカヤック]]などができる海洋体験施設。 * [[宗像大社]]中津宮 - 世界遺産宗像大社の構成要素の一つ。宗像三姉妹の二女タギツヒメを祀る。 * [[御嶽神社 (宗像市)|御嶽神社]] - 中津宮の奥宮、元宮で古代祭祀が行われていた聖地で大島御嶽遺跡がある。 * 御嶽山 - 島内最高峰で御嶽神社が位置している。山頂は展望台となっている。 * [[安倍宗任]]の墓所 - 宗任は当地に流されて晩年を過ごしたとされる。 * 夢の小夜島 - 島の東側にある、松に覆われた小さな島。室町時代、連歌師の[[宗祇]]はこの地を訪れ和歌に詠んでいる。干潮時のみ近寄ることが可能。 * かんす海水浴場 - 夢の小夜島近くにある海水浴場。 * 大島交流館 - 大島および沖ノ島の歴史や文化などを紹介する施設。 * 沖津宮遥拝所 - 世界遺産宗像大社の構成要素の一つ。遠く沖津宮の御神体島である沖ノ島を拝する社殿。 * 風車展望所 - 島内屈指の絶景スポットで、晴れた日には沖ノ島が見える。 * 下関要塞大島砲台跡 - 風車展望所に近接。地下弾薬庫や観測所跡が残る。日本海海戦・戦死者慰霊碑が建てられている。 * 大島牧場 - 風車展望所に近接。[[乗馬]]体験ができる。 * 神崎 - 島の北西部にある岬。先端には旧[[陸軍省]]の設置した碑がある。 * 馬蹄岩 - 神崎にあり、宗像大神が馬に乗り島々に飛び立った伝説から名がつけられた。岩には数多くの[[盃状穴]]が存在している。 * 大島灯台 - 神崎の近くにある白亜の[[灯台]]。景勝地として知られる。 * 三浦洞窟 - 大島灯台の近くにある洞窟。[[隠れキリシタン]]伝説がある。 ファイル:Umingu Oshima.jpg|うみんぐ大島 ファイル:Street view near Oshima Port on Oshima Island, Munakata, Fukuoka.JPG|大島港付近の町並み ファイル:Grand torii of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|[[宗像大社]]中津宮の鳥居 ファイル:Abe no Muneto tomb.jpg|安倍宗任の墓所 File:Yumenosayoshima and Kansu Beach.jpg|夢の小夜島 ファイル:Oshima Culture Center.jpg|大島交流館 ファイル:宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 - panoramio.jpg|宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 ファイル:大島灯台 - panoramio.jpg|大島灯台 ファイル:Kamizaki Oshima.jpg|神崎 === 宿泊施設 === 島内に数件の民宿と旅館がある。また島の西海岸には大島キャンプ場がある。 == 祭事 == * [[みあれ祭]] - 宗像大社の秋季大祭である田島放生会の始まりを告げる祭事。三女神が年に一度一緒に奉斎される。 == 産業 == [[漁業]]が中心だが、小規模な[[農業]]もあり、[[甘夏]]・[[アカモク]]・[[海塩]]等が特産品として知られる。また、島の西側の大島牧場で[[黒毛和種|黒毛和牛]]を飼育している。 == 交通 == === 陸上交通 === [[福岡県道541号大島循環線|県道541号線]]が島南東部のフェリーターミナル周辺部の中心集落を通り内陸部を一周する形で敷設されているほか、中心集落内や海岸部などへの道路もある。島内をめぐる観光路線バス「グランシマール」（[[西鉄バス宗像]]）、「みあれ号」（みなとタクシー）が運行している。タクシーは2008年4月にみなとタクシーが島内に営業所を設置し、2台を配置しており(現在は1台)通常はフェリーターミナルにいる。また、フェリーターミナル等でレンタサイクルを借りることもできる。 === 水上交通 === 九州本土の宗像市・神湊港より[[大島港 (福岡県)|大島港]]まで[[宗像市営渡船|市営フェリー]]「フェリーおおしま」で25分、旅客船「しおかぜ」で15分。ダイヤおよび運航状況については宗像市のウェブサイトに記載がある。 その他に民営の海上タクシーなどがある。 神湊港までは[[東郷駅]]から[[西鉄バス宗像|西鉄バス]]神湊波止場ゆきに乗車し終点下車。マイカーの場合、[[九州自動車道]][[若宮インターチェンジ]]より19㎞、同[[古賀インターチェンジ]]より17㎞。 ファイル:Oosimakou.jpg|大島港渡船ターミナル（2009年） ファイル:Munakata City Ferry Oshima.jpg|フェリーおおしま（2018年） == 脚注 == == 関連項目 == * [[日本の地理]] * [[日本の島の一覧]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Ōshima, Munakata}} * [https://maps.gsi.go.jp/#14/33.897741/130.433164/&base=std&ls=std&disp=1&vs=c1j0h0k0l0u0t0z0r0s0m0f1 地理院地図] {{日本の指定離島}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:おおしま}} [[Category:宗像市の地理]] [[Category:宗像市の町・字]] [[Category:福岡県の島]] [[Category:日本海の島]] [[Category:対馬海峡]]
