It is located in the prefecture of [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], in the southwestern part of the country, about {{formatnum:900}} km west of [[Tokyo (the capital city of Japan)|Tokyo]], the capital of the country. It covers an area of approximately {{formatnum:7.5}} square kilometers. The terrain of Ō Shima is flat.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The highest point of the island is {{formatnum:206}} meters above sea level. It spans 3.1 km from north to south and 4.0 km from east to west.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The climate is [[temperate]]. The average temperature is {{formatnum:15}} [[°C]]. The warmest month is August, at {{formatnum:24}} [[°C]], and the coldest is February, at {{formatnum:6}} °C. The average annual rainfall is {{formatnum:2130}} millimeters. The wettest month is July, with {{formatnum:410}} millimeters of rain, and the driest is January, with {{formatnum:47}} millimeters. {| class="climate chart" |- | '''Ō Shima Climate Data''' | January | 5 | 8 | 47 | February | 4 | 7 | 157| March | 6 | 13 | 136| April | 10 | 17 | 120| May | 14 | 20 | 89| June | 15 | 21 | 294| July | 20 | 22 | 410| August | 23 | 26 | 383| September | 19 | 21 | 146| October | 17 | 21 | 126| November | 12 | 16 | 124| December | 7 | 11 | 98|- | colspan="13" | Data source: |} == Geography == [[File:Oshima_Island,_Munakata_Fukuoka_Aerial_photograph.2010.jpg|alt=Ōshima aerial photograph.|thumb|280x280px]]
Created by combining 26 images taken on June 3, 2010. {{ill|GSI Aerial Photograph|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Ōshima is located about 6.5 {{ill|kilometers|ja|キロメートル|qq=draft|qq=draft}} northwest of the Konominato Port on the Munakata mainland. About 5 km to the east lies {{ill|Jinoshima|ja|地島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Together with Jinoshima and {{ill|Okinoshima|ja|沖ノ島|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it marks the boundary between {{ill|Genkai Sea|ja|玄界灘|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|qq=draft|qq=draft}}—the sea on the west side of the island is Genkai-nada, and on the east side is Hibiki-nada. Its total area is 7.17 km{{sup|2}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001015648.pdf List of Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Areas]}} – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, National and Regional Policy Bureau, Remote Islands Development Division, making it the largest of the remote islands in Fukuoka Prefecture. Much of the island is hilly with steep terrain, and the highest peak is Mitake (224 m) in the island’s center. On the eastern side of the island is Ōshima Port, where ferries connect to the mainland, and a ferry terminal is located there. Slightly south of the ferry terminal is Ōshima Fishing Port, while Miyazaki Fishing Port is to the northeast. Homes and settlements are concentrated around these port areas. The population is 540 with 278 households (from the Reiwa 2 {{ill|National Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本)|lt=National Census|lt_ja=国勢調査|qq=draft|qq=draft}}). The island has {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a {{ill|compulsory education school|ja|義務教育学校|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == History == In [[1889]] (Meiji 22), under the {{ill|Town and Village Act|ja|町村制|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it became {{ill|Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島村 (福岡県)|lt=Oshima Village|lt_ja=大島村|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Munakata District|ja|宗像郡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. From May 27 to 28, 1905, the {{ill|Battle of Tsushima|ja|日本海海戦|qq=draft|qq=draft}} took place offshore, and many Russian soldiers’ bodies washed ashore on Ōshima.[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ Katsuya Kodama “Memorial Service for the Russo-Japanese War on Munakata City’s Ōshima ~A New Bridge of Friendship and Peace between Japan and Russia!~” (November 3, 2013)] (Accessed January 16, 2018) Residents are said to have buried them respectfully. On March 28, 2005, the village was merged into Munakata City. Beginning in 1935 (Shōwa 10), as part of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, a battery was constructed on the island’s northern coast (Ōshima Battery) equipped with four {{ill|Type 45 15 cm Cannon|ja|四五式十五糎加農砲|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Associated facilities included an observation post, underground ammunition depot, a mobile 150 cm searchlight, and a power station. After the war, these cannons were removed, but their mounts and other remnants remain. Since 2012, a Japan–Russia joint memorial service has been held for those who died in the Battle of Tsushima, and in November 2013, a monument to the war dead was erected in front of the former Ōshima Battery. In July 2017 ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft}} 29), Nakatsumiya and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho were inscribed as part of the “{{ill|Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|ja|「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” World Heritage Site. == Religious Facilities == At the summit of Mt. Mitake stands an observation platform and the Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) of Nakatsumiya, called {{ill|Mitake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In ancient times, this was a ritual site for Nakatsumiya. Nearby is the Orihime-Hikoboshi Shrine, and local tradition holds that this place is the birthplace of Japan’s Tanabata legend. Near the port is Nakatsumiya of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the {{ill|The Three Female Deities of Munakata|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. On the north side of the island is the {{ill|Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|ja|沖津宮遙拝所|lt=Okitsumiya Yohaisho|lt_ja=沖津宮遙拝所|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, where one can worship the distant island of Okinoshima, home to Okitsumiya, which is forbidden to women. On clear days, one can faintly see Okinoshima from there, but it cannot be seen on cloudy or rainy days. These two sites are part of the “Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region,” a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. Additionally, Ōshima is traditionally said to be the place where {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft}} spent his final years in exile. It is also on the route of the {{ill|Kyushu Olle|ja|九州オルレ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} hiking course. == Major Facilities and Attractions on the Island == === Main Facilities === * Municipal Office – Munakata City Ōshima Administrative Center * School – {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * Nursery – Ōshima Nursery School === Tourist Attractions === * Umingu Ōshima – A marine experience facility offering {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Sea kayaking|ja|シーカヤック|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. * {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} Nakatsumiya – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. Dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the Munakata Three Sisters. * {{ill|Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|ja|御嶽神社 (宗像市)|lt=Mitake Shrine|lt_ja=御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – The Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) and original sacred site of Nakatsumiya from ancient times, known as the Ōshima Mitake Archaeological Site. * Mt. Mitake – The highest peak on the island, home to Mitake Shrine at its summit. The summit has an observation platform. * Grave of {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – According to tradition, Munetō was exiled here and spent his final days on the island. * Yume-no-Sayoshima – A small island covered by pines on the east side of Ōshima. In the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Renga poet|ja|連歌師|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{ill|Iio Sōgi|ja|宗祇|qq=draft|qq=draft}} visited and composed waka poetry about it. It is accessible only at low tide. * Kansu Beach – A swimming beach near Yume-no-Sayoshima. * Ōshima Exchange Hall (Ōshima Kōryūkan) – A facility introducing the history and culture of Ōshima and Okinoshima. * Okitsumiya Yohaisho – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. A {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|qq=draft|qq=draft}} for the sacred island of Okinoshima, the location of Okitsumiya. * Windmill Observation Deck – Known as one of the best scenic spots on the island. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|qq=draft|qq=draft}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|qq=draft|qq=draft}} legend. File:Umingu Oshima.jpg|Umingu Ōshima File:Street view near Oshima Port on Oshima Island, Munakata, Fukuoka.JPG|Townscape near Ōshima Port File:Grand torii of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Torii of Munakata Taisha Nakatsumiya File:Abe no Muneto tomb.jpg|Grave of Abe no Munetō File:Yumenosayoshima and Kansu Beach.jpg|Yume-no-Sayoshima File:Oshima Culture Center.jpg|Ōshima Exchange Hall File:宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 - panoramio.jpg|Okitsumiya Yohaisho (Munakata Taisha) File:大島灯台 - panoramio.jpg|Ōshima Lighthouse File:Kamizaki Oshima.jpg|Kamizaki === Accommodations === There are a few inns and guesthouses on the island. A campground called Ōshima Campground is located on the island’s western coast. == Festivals == * {{ill|Miare Festival|ja|みあれ祭|qq=draft|qq=draft}} – The autumn grand festival of Munakata Taisha, marking the beginning of the Tashima Hōjōe (harvest festival). It is the one time of the year when all three goddesses are enshrined together. == Industry == {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft}} is the main industry, but small-scale {{ill|Agriculture|ja|農業|qq=draft|qq=draft}} also exists, and specialty products include {{ill|Amanatsu|ja|甘夏|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Akamoku|ja|アカモク|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, and {{ill|Sea salt|ja|海塩|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. In addition, {{ill|Japanese Black|ja|黒毛和種|qq=draft|qq=draft}} cattle are raised on the western side of the island at Ōshima Ranch. == Transportation == === Land Transportation === {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|ja|福岡県道541号大島循環線|qq=draft|qq=draft}} runs around the central settlement area near the ferry terminal in the southeast and circles the interior of the island, with additional roads leading into the central settlement and coastal areas. Two sightseeing buses operate around the island: the “Granshima-ru” (run by {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|ja|西鉄バス宗像|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and the “Miare-gō” (operated by Minato Taxi). In April 2008, Minato Taxi set up an office on the island with two taxis (currently one), usually stationed at the ferry terminal. Bicycle rentals are also available at the ferry terminal and elsewhere. === Maritime Transportation === From the mainland’s Konominato Port in Munakata City to {{ill|Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島港 (福岡県)|lt=Ōshima Port|lt_ja=大島港|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, it takes 25 minutes on the municipal ferry “{{ill|Munakata Municipal Ferry|ja|宗像市営渡船|lt=Ferry Oshima|lt_ja=フェリーおおしま|qq=draft|qq=draft}}” or 15 minutes on the passenger boat “Shiokaze.” The schedule and current operating status are posted on Munakata City’s website. There are also private sea taxis. To reach Konominato Port, take the bus bound for Konominato Wharf from {{ill|Tōgō Station|ja|東郷駅|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Nishitetsu Bus Munakata); get off at the final stop. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. File:Oosimakou.jpg|Ōshima Port Ferry Terminal (2009) File:Munakata City Ferry Oshima.jpg|Ferry Oshima (2018) == References == == See Also == * {{ill|Geography of Japan|ja|日本の地理|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|List of islands of Japan|ja|日本の島の一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Ōshima, Munakata}} * [https://maps.gsi.go.jp/#14/33.897741/130.433164/&base=std&ls=std&disp=1&vs=c1j0h0k0l0u0t0z0r0s0m0f1 GSI Maps] {{ill|Designated Islands of Japan|ja|日本の指定離島|qq=draft|qq=draft}} {{Normdaten}} == References == [{{Geonameslink|gnid=1853774|name=o%20shima}} Ō Shima] at [{{Geonamesabout}} Geonames.org (cc-by)]; post updated 2015-06-15; database downloaded 2017-02-07 {{Cite web |url= {{Viewfinderlink}}|title= Viewfinder Panoramas Digital elevation Model|date= 2015-06-21|format= }} {{Cite web |url= http://neo.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/dataset_index.php|title= NASA Earth Observations Data Set Index|access-date= ] }}January 30, 2016 |publisher= NASA}} {{Cite web |url= http://neo.sci.gsfc.nasa.gov/view.php?datasetId=TRMM_3B43M|title= NASA Earth Observations: Rainfall (1 month - TRMM)|access-date= ] }}January 30, 2016 |publisher= NASA/Tropical Rainfall Monitoring Mission}} {{translated page|ja|大島 (福岡県)|version=101944569|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:Ōshima (Fukuoka)]] [[Category:Geography of Munakata City]] [[Category:Towns and Districts of Munakata City]] [[Category:Islands of Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Islands of the Sea of Japan]] [[Category:Tsushima Strait]] [[Category:deprecated 11 open]] [[Category:11 close]] [[Category:subst:PAGENAME}]] [[Category:Islands in Fukuoka Prefecture]] [[Category:Islands of Japan larger than 5 square kilometers]] }} [[ceb:Ō_Shima_(pulo_sa_Hapon,_Fukuoka-ken)]] [[ceb:Ō Shima (pulo sa Hapon, Fukuoka-ken)]] [[sn:Ōshima (Fukuoka)]] [[fa:اوشیما_(استان_فوکوئوکا)]] [[ja:大島_(福岡県)]] [[fa:اوشیما (استان فوکوئوکا)]] [[ja:大島 (福岡県)]]

{{Location map|Japan |float=right |width=300 | caption = Location of Ō Shima in Japan. | label = Ō Shima|position=right|background=white|lat=33.90222|long=130.42414}} '''Ōshima''' (大島) is an {{ill|Island|ja|島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Island|qq=}} (an inhabited island) in {{ill|Munakata City|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}}, facing the boundary between {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibiki-nada|qq=}} and {{ill|Genkai-nada|ja|玄界灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genkai-nada|qq=}}. As part of the Chikuzen Islands area, it is designated as a Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Area under the {{ill|Remote Islands Development Act|ja|離島振興法|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Remote Islands Development Act|qq=}}.[https://www.mlit.go.jp/kokudoseisaku/chirit/content/001619210.pdf Fukuoka Prefecture "Fukuoka Prefecture Remote Islands Development Plan (FY2023 – FY2032)"] – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (Accessed September 23, 2024) The island’s area is about 7.17 {{ill|square kilometers|ja|平方キロメートル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square kilometers|qq=}}. It is also known as Chikuzen-Ōshima and is one of the {{ill|the Seven Inlets of Munakata|ja|宗像七浦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/the Seven Inlets of Munakata|qq=}}, home to the Middle Shrine (Nakatsumiya) of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}} and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho, which are part of a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Heritage Site|qq=}}. Slightly south of the ferry terminal is Ōshima Fishing Port, while Miyazaki Fishing Port is to the northeast. Homes and settlements are concentrated around these port areas. The population is 540 with 278 households (from the Reiwa 2 {{ill|National Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本)|lt=National Census|lt_ja=国勢調査|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Census (Japan)|qq=}}). The island has {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|qq=}}, a {{ill|compulsory education school|ja|義務教育学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/compulsory education school|qq=}}. == History == In [[1889]] (Meiji 22), under the {{ill|Town and Village Act|ja|町村制|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Town and Village Act|qq=}}, it became {{ill|Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島村 (福岡県)|lt=Oshima Village|lt_ja=大島村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|qq=}} in {{ill|Munakata District|ja|宗像郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata District|qq=}}. From May 27 to 28, 1905, the {{ill|Battle of Tsushima|ja|日本海海戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Tsushima|qq=}} took place offshore, and many Russian soldiers’ bodies washed ashore on Ōshima.[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ Katsuya Kodama “Memorial Service for the Russo-Japanese War on Munakata City’s Ōshima ~A New Bridge of Friendship and Peace between Japan and Russia!~” (November 3, 2013)] (Accessed January 16, 2018) Residents are said to have buried them respectfully. On March 28, 2005, the village was merged into Munakata City. Beginning in 1935 (Shōwa 10), as part of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimonoseki Fortress|qq=}}, a battery was constructed on the island’s northern coast (Ōshima Battery) equipped with four {{ill|Type 45 15 cm Cannon|ja|四五式十五糎加農砲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Type 45 15 cm Cannon|qq=}}. Associated facilities included an observation post, underground ammunition depot, a mobile 150 cm searchlight, and a power station. After the war, these cannons were removed, but their mounts and other remnants remain. Since 2012, a Japan–Russia joint memorial service has been held for those who died in the Battle of Tsushima, and in November 2013, a monument to the war dead was erected in front of the former Ōshima Battery. In July 2017 ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heisei|qq=}} 29), Nakatsumiya and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho were inscribed as part of the “{{ill|Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|ja|「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|qq=}}” World Heritage Site. == Religious Facilities == At the summit of Mt. Mitake stands an observation platform and the Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) of Nakatsumiya, called {{ill|Mitake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitake Shrine|qq=}}. In ancient times, this was a ritual site for Nakatsumiya. Nearby is the Orihime-Hikoboshi Shrine, and local tradition holds that this place is the birthplace of Japan’s Tanabata legend. Near the port is Nakatsumiya of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}}, dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the {{ill|The Three Female Deities of Munakata|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/The Three Female Deities of Munakata|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=}}. On the north side of the island is the {{ill|Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|ja|沖津宮遙拝所|lt=Okitsumiya Yohaisho|lt_ja=沖津宮遙拝所|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|qq=}}, where one can worship the distant island of Okinoshima, home to Okitsumiya, which is forbidden to women. On clear days, one can faintly see Okinoshima from there, but it cannot be seen on cloudy or rainy days. These two sites are part of the “Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region,” a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Heritage Site|qq=}}. Additionally, Ōshima is traditionally said to be the place where {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Munetō|qq=}} spent his final years in exile. It is also on the route of the {{ill|Kyushu Olle|ja|九州オルレ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Olle|qq=}} hiking course. == Major Facilities and Attractions on the Island == === Main Facilities === * Municipal Office – Munakata City Ōshima Administrative Center * School – {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|qq=}} * Nursery – Ōshima Nursery School === Tourist Attractions === * Umingu Ōshima – A marine experience facility offering {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fishing|qq=}} and {{ill|Sea kayaking|ja|シーカヤック|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sea kayaking|qq=}}. * {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}} Nakatsumiya – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. Dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the Munakata Three Sisters. * {{ill|Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|ja|御嶽神社 (宗像市)|lt=Mitake Shrine|lt_ja=御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|qq=}} – The Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) and original sacred site of Nakatsumiya from ancient times, known as the Ōshima Mitake Archaeological Site. * Mt. Mitake – The highest peak on the island, home to Mitake Shrine at its summit. The summit has an observation platform. * Grave of {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Munetō|qq=}} – According to tradition, Munetō was exiled here and spent his final days on the island. * Yume-no-Sayoshima – A small island covered by pines on the east side of Ōshima. In the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Renga poet|ja|連歌師|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Renga poet|qq=}} {{ill|Iio Sōgi|ja|宗祇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iio Sōgi|qq=}} visited and composed waka poetry about it. It is accessible only at low tide. * Kansu Beach – A swimming beach near Yume-no-Sayoshima. * Ōshima Exchange Hall (Ōshima Kōryūkan) – A facility introducing the history and culture of Ōshima and Okinoshima. * Okitsumiya Yohaisho – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. A {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haisho|qq=}} for the sacred island of Okinoshima, the location of Okitsumiya. * Windmill Observation Deck – Known as one of the best scenic spots on the island. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimonoseki Fortress|qq=}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Army|qq=}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hidden Christian|qq=}} legend. File:Umingu Oshima.jpg|Umingu Ōshima File:Street view near Oshima Port on Oshima Island, Munakata, Fukuoka.JPG|Townscape near Ōshima Port File:Grand torii of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Torii of Munakata Taisha Nakatsumiya File:Abe no Muneto tomb.jpg|Grave of Abe no Munetō File:Yumenosayoshima and Kansu Beach.jpg|Yume-no-Sayoshima File:Oshima Culture Center.jpg|Ōshima Exchange Hall File:宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 - panoramio.jpg|Okitsumiya Yohaisho (Munakata Taisha) File:大島灯台 - panoramio.jpg|Ōshima Lighthouse File:Kamizaki Oshima.jpg|Kamizaki === Accommodations === There are a few inns and guesthouses on the island. A campground called Ōshima Campground is located on the island’s western coast. == Festivals == * {{ill|Miare Festival|ja|みあれ祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miare Festival|qq=}} – The autumn grand festival of Munakata Taisha, marking the beginning of the Tashima Hōjōe (harvest festival). It is the one time of the year when all three goddesses are enshrined together. == Industry == {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fishing|qq=}} is the main industry, but small-scale {{ill|Agriculture|ja|農業|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agriculture|qq=}} also exists, and specialty products include {{ill|Amanatsu|ja|甘夏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanatsu|qq=}}, {{ill|Akamoku|ja|アカモク|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akamoku|qq=}}, and {{ill|Sea salt|ja|海塩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sea salt|qq=}}. In addition, {{ill|Japanese Black|ja|黒毛和種|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Black|qq=}} cattle are raised on the western side of the island at Ōshima Ranch. == Transportation == === Land Transportation === {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|ja|福岡県道541号大島循環線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|qq=}} runs around the central settlement area near the ferry terminal in the southeast and circles the interior of the island, with additional roads leading into the central settlement and coastal areas. Two sightseeing buses operate around the island: the “Granshima-ru” (run by {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|ja|西鉄バス宗像|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|qq=}}) and the “Miare-gō” (operated by Minato Taxi). In April 2008, Minato Taxi set up an office on the island with two taxis (currently one), usually stationed at the ferry terminal. Bicycle rentals are also available at the ferry terminal and elsewhere. === Maritime Transportation === From the mainland’s Konominato Port in Munakata City to {{ill|Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島港 (福岡県)|lt=Ōshima Port|lt_ja=大島港|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|qq=}}, it takes 25 minutes on the municipal ferry “{{ill|Munakata Municipal Ferry|ja|宗像市営渡船|lt=Ferry Oshima|lt_ja=フェリーおおしま|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Municipal Ferry|qq=}}” or 15 minutes on the passenger boat “Shiokaze.” The schedule and current operating status are posted on Munakata City’s website. There are also private sea taxis. To reach Konominato Port, take the bus bound for Konominato Wharf from {{ill|Tōgō Station|ja|東郷駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōgō Station|qq=}} (Nishitetsu Bus Munakata); get off at the final stop. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakamiya Interchange|qq=}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koga Interchange|qq=}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Expressway|qq=}}. File:Oosimakou.jpg|Ōshima Port Ferry Terminal (2009) File:Munakata City Ferry Oshima.jpg|Ferry Oshima (2018) == References == == See Also == * {{ill|Geography of Japan|ja|日本の地理|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Geography of Japan|qq=}} * {{ill|List of islands of Japan|ja|日本の島の一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of islands of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Ōshima, Munakata}} * [https://maps.gsi.go.jp/#14/33.897741/130.433164/&base=std&ls=std&disp=1&vs=c1j0h0k0l0u0t0z0r0s0m0f1 GSI Maps] {{ill|Designated Islands of Japan|ja|日本の指定離島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Designated Islands of Japan|qq=}} {{Normdaten}} == References == [{{Geonameslink|gnid=1853774|name=o%20shima}} Ō Shima] at [{{Geonamesabout}} Geonames.org (cc-by)]; {{Location map|Japan |float=right |width=300 | caption = Location of Ō Shima in Japan. | label = Ō Shima|position=right|background=white|lat=33.90222|long=130.42414}} '''Ōshima''' (大島) is an {{ill|Island|ja|島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Island|qq=}} (an inhabited island) in {{ill|Munakata City|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}}, facing the boundary between {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibiki-nada|qq=}} and {{ill|Genkai-nada|ja|玄界灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genkai-nada|qq=}}. As part of the Chikuzen Islands area, it is designated as a Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Area under the {{ill|Remote Islands Development Act|ja|離島振興法|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Remote Islands Development Act|qq=}}.[https://www.mlit.go.jp/kokudoseisaku/chirit/content/001619210.pdf Fukuoka Prefecture "Fukuoka Prefecture Remote Islands Development Plan (FY2023 – FY2032)"] – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (Accessed September 23, 2024) The island’s area is about 7.17 {{ill|square kilometers|ja|平方キロメートル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square kilometers|qq=}}. It is also known as Chikuzen-Ōshima and is one of the {{ill|the Seven Inlets of Munakata|ja|宗像七浦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/the Seven Inlets of Munakata|qq=}}, home to the Middle Shrine (Nakatsumiya) of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}} and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho, which are part of a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Heritage Site|qq=}}. Its catchphrase is “Island that Protects the Gods.” == Overview == {{Created by bot|Lsjbot|Japan|date=2017-02}} :''For other places with the same name, see [[Ō Shima]].'' {{geobox | 1 = Island | name = Ō Shima | native_name = 大島 | other_name = Ō Sima | category = Island | etymology = | nickname = | image = | image_caption = | country = {{flag|Japan}} | country_flag = true | state = [[Fukuoka Prefecture]] | state_type = Prefecture | region = | region_type = | district = | district_type = | municipality = | municipality_type = | parent = | range = | range_type = Archipelago | border = | part = | city = | capital = | landmark = | river = | location = | lat_d = 33.90222 | lat_m = | lat_s = | lat_NS = | long_d = 130.42414 | long_m = | long_s = | long_EW = | highest = | highest_location = | highest_region = | highest_country = | highest_elevation = | highest_lat_d = | highest_lat_m = | highest_lat_s = | highest_lat_NS = | highest_long_d = | highest_long_m = | highest_long_s = | highest_long_EW = | length = | length_orientation = | width = | width_orientation = | height = | area = 7.46 | population = | population_date = | population_note = | population_density = | population_density_note = | public = | access = | timezone = [[Japan Standard Time|JST]] | utc_offset = +9 | timezone_DST = | utc_offset_DST = | postal_code = | area_code = | code = | free = | free_type = | map = | map_caption = | map_locator_x = | map_locator_y = | footnotes = | other_name1 = Ō-shima | other_name2 = 筑前大島 | other_name3 = Tchikuzen-Ōshima | elevation = 128 | timezone_label = Asia/Tokyo | geonames = 1853774 }} [[Island]] '''Ō Shima''' ([[Japanese]]: '''大島''', '''筑前大島''') is in [[Japan]]. It is located in the prefecture of [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], in the southwestern part of the country, about {{formatnum:900}} km west of [[Tokyo (the capital city of Japan)|Tokyo]], the capital of the country. It covers an area of approximately {{formatnum:7.5}} square kilometers. The terrain of Ō Shima is flat.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The highest point of the island is {{formatnum:206}} meters above sea level. It spans 3.1 km from north to south and 4.0 km from east to west.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The climate is [[temperate]]. The average temperature is {{formatnum:15}} [[°C]]. The warmest month is August, at {{formatnum:24}} [[°C]], and the coldest is February, at {{formatnum:6}} °C. The average annual rainfall is {{formatnum:2130}} millimeters. The wettest month is July, with {{formatnum:410}} millimeters of rain, and the driest is January, with {{formatnum:47}} millimeters. {| class="climate chart" |- | '''Ō Shima Climate Data''' | January | 5 | 8 | 47 | February | 4 | 7 | 157| March | 6 | 13 | 136| April | 10 | 17 | 120| May | 14 | 20 | 89| June | 15 | 21 | 294| July | 20 | 22 | 410| August | 23 | 26 | 383| September | 19 | 21 | 146| October | 17 | 21 | 126| November | 12 | 16 | 124| December | 7 | 11 | 98|- | colspan="13" | Data source: |} == Geography == [[File:Oshima_Island,_Munakata_Fukuoka_Aerial_photograph.2010.jpg|alt=Ōshima aerial photograph.|thumb|280x280px]]
Created by combining 26 images taken on June 3, 2010. {{ill|GSI Aerial Photograph|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/GSI Aerial Photograph|qq=}}. Ōshima is located about 6.5 {{ill|kilometers|ja|キロメートル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kilometers|qq=}} northwest of the Konominato Port on the Munakata mainland. About 5 km to the east lies {{ill|Jinoshima|ja|地島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinoshima|qq=}}. Together with Jinoshima and {{ill|Okinoshima|ja|沖ノ島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okinoshima|qq=}}, it marks the boundary between {{ill|Genkai Sea|ja|玄界灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genkai Sea|qq=}} and {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibiki-nada|qq=}}—the sea on the west side of the island is Genkai-nada, and on the east side is Hibiki-nada. Its total area is 7.17 km{{sup|2}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001015648.pdf List of Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Areas]}} – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, National and Regional Policy Bureau, Remote Islands Development Division, making it the largest of the remote islands in Fukuoka Prefecture. Much of the island is hilly with steep terrain, and the highest peak is Mitake (224 m) in the island’s center. On the eastern side of the island is Ōshima Port, where ferries connect to the mainland, and a ferry terminal is located there. Slightly south of the ferry terminal is Ōshima Fishing Port, while Miyazaki Fishing Port is to the northeast. Homes and settlements are concentrated around these port areas. The population is 540 with 278 households (from the Reiwa 2 {{ill|National Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本)|lt=National Census|lt_ja=国勢調査|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Census (Japan)|qq=}}). The island has {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|qq=}}, a {{ill|compulsory education school|ja|義務教育学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/compulsory education school|qq=}}. == History == In [[1889]] (Meiji 22), under the {{ill|Town and Village Act|ja|町村制|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Town and Village Act|qq=}}, it became {{ill|Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島村 (福岡県)|lt=Oshima Village|lt_ja=大島村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|qq=}} in {{ill|Munakata District|ja|宗像郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata District|qq=}}. From May 27 to 28, 1905, the {{ill|Battle of Tsushima|ja|日本海海戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Tsushima|qq=}} took place offshore, and many Russian soldiers’ bodies washed ashore on Ōshima.[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ Katsuya Kodama “Memorial Service for the Russo-Japanese War on Munakata City’s Ōshima ~A New Bridge of Friendship and Peace between Japan and Russia!~” (November 3, 2013)] (Accessed January 16, 2018) Residents are said to have buried them respectfully. On March 28, 2005, the village was merged into Munakata City. Beginning in 1935 (Shōwa 10), as part of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimonoseki Fortress|qq=}}, a battery was constructed on the island’s northern coast (Ōshima Battery) equipped with four {{ill|Type 45 15 cm Cannon|ja|四五式十五糎加農砲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Type 45 15 cm Cannon|qq=}}. Associated facilities included an observation post, underground ammunition depot, a mobile 150 cm searchlight, and a power station. After the war, these cannons were removed, but their mounts and other remnants remain. Since 2012, a Japan–Russia joint memorial service has been held for those who died in the Battle of Tsushima, and in November 2013, a monument to the war dead was erected in front of the former Ōshima Battery. In July 2017 ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heisei|qq=}} 29), Nakatsumiya and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho were inscribed as part of the “{{ill|Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|ja|「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|qq=}}” World Heritage Site. == Religious Facilities == At the summit of Mt. Mitake stands an observation platform and the Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) of Nakatsumiya, called {{ill|Mitake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitake Shrine|qq=}}. In ancient times, this was a ritual site for Nakatsumiya. Nearby is the Orihime-Hikoboshi Shrine, and local tradition holds that this place is the birthplace of Japan’s Tanabata legend. Near the port is Nakatsumiya of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}}, dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the {{ill|The Three Female Deities of Munakata|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/The Three Female Deities of Munakata|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=}}. On the north side of the island is the {{ill|Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|ja|沖津宮遙拝所|lt=Okitsumiya Yohaisho|lt_ja=沖津宮遙拝所|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|qq=}}, where one can worship the distant island of Okinoshima, home to Okitsumiya, which is forbidden to women. On clear days, one can faintly see Okinoshima from there, but it cannot be seen on cloudy or rainy days. These two sites are part of the “Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region,” a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Heritage Site|qq=}}. Additionally, Ōshima is traditionally said to be the place where {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Munetō|qq=}} spent his final years in exile. It is also on the route of the {{ill|Kyushu Olle|ja|九州オルレ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Olle|qq=}} hiking course. == Major Facilities and Attractions on the Island == === Main Facilities === * Municipal Office – Munakata City Ōshima Administrative Center * School – {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|qq=}} * Nursery – Ōshima Nursery School === Tourist Attractions === * Umingu Ōshima – A marine experience facility offering {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fishing|qq=}} and {{ill|Sea kayaking|ja|シーカヤック|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sea kayaking|qq=}}. * {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}} Nakatsumiya – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. Dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the Munakata Three Sisters. * {{ill|Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|ja|御嶽神社 (宗像市)|lt=Mitake Shrine|lt_ja=御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|qq=}} – The Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) and original sacred site of Nakatsumiya from ancient times, known as the Ōshima Mitake Archaeological Site. * Mt. Mitake – The highest peak on the island, home to Mitake Shrine at its summit. The summit has an observation platform. * Grave of {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Munetō|qq=}} – According to tradition, Munetō was exiled here and spent his final days on the island. * Yume-no-Sayoshima – A small island covered by pines on the east side of Ōshima. In the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Renga poet|ja|連歌師|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Renga poet|qq=}} {{ill|Iio Sōgi|ja|宗祇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iio Sōgi|qq=}} visited and composed waka poetry about it. It is accessible only at low tide. * Kansu Beach – A swimming beach near Yume-no-Sayoshima. * Ōshima Exchange Hall (Ōshima Kōryūkan) – A facility introducing the history and culture of Ōshima and Okinoshima. * Okitsumiya Yohaisho – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. A {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haisho|qq=}} for the sacred island of Okinoshima, the location of Okitsumiya. * Windmill Observation Deck – Known as one of the best scenic spots on the island. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimonoseki Fortress|qq=}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Army|qq=}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hidden Christian|qq=}} legend. File:Umingu Oshima.jpg|Umingu Ōshima File:Street view near Oshima Port on Oshima Island, Munakata, Fukuoka.JPG|Townscape near Ōshima Port File:Grand torii of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Torii of Munakata Taisha Nakatsumiya File:Abe no Muneto tomb.jpg|Grave of Abe no Munetō File:Yumenosayoshima and Kansu Beach.jpg|Yume-no-Sayoshima File:Oshima Culture Center.jpg|Ōshima Exchange Hall File:宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 - panoramio.jpg|Okitsumiya Yohaisho (Munakata Taisha) File:大島灯台 - panoramio.jpg|Ōshima Lighthouse File:Kamizaki Oshima.jpg|Kamizaki === Accommodations === There are a few inns and guesthouses on the island. A campground called Ōshima Campground is located on the island’s western coast. == Festivals == * {{ill|Miare Festival|ja|みあれ祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miare Festival|qq=}} – The autumn grand festival of Munakata Taisha, marking the beginning of the Tashima Hōjōe (harvest festival). It is the one time of the year when all three goddesses are enshrined together. == Industry == {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fishing|qq=}} is the main industry, but small-scale {{ill|Agriculture|ja|農業|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agriculture|qq=}} also exists, and specialty products include {{ill|Amanatsu|ja|甘夏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanatsu|qq=}}, {{ill|Akamoku|ja|アカモク|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akamoku|qq=}}, and {{ill|Sea salt|ja|海塩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sea salt|qq=}}. In addition, {{ill|Japanese Black|ja|黒毛和種|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Black|qq=}} cattle are raised on the western side of the island at Ōshima Ranch. == Transportation == === Land Transportation === {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|ja|福岡県道541号大島循環線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|qq=}} runs around the central settlement area near the ferry terminal in the southeast and circles the interior of the island, with additional roads leading into the central settlement and coastal areas. Two sightseeing buses operate around the island: the “Granshima-ru” (run by {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|ja|西鉄バス宗像|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|qq=}}) and the “Miare-gō” (operated by Minato Taxi). In April 2008, Minato Taxi set up an office on the island with two taxis (currently one), usually stationed at the ferry terminal. Bicycle rentals are also available at the ferry terminal and elsewhere. === Maritime Transportation === From the mainland’s Konominato Port in Munakata City to {{ill|Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島港 (福岡県)|lt=Ōshima Port|lt_ja=大島港|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|qq=}}, it takes 25 minutes on the municipal ferry “{{ill|Munakata Municipal Ferry|ja|宗像市営渡船|lt=Ferry Oshima|lt_ja=フェリーおおしま|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Municipal Ferry|qq=}}” or 15 minutes on the passenger boat “Shiokaze.” The schedule and current operating status are posted on Munakata City’s website. There are also private sea taxis. To reach Konominato Port, take the bus bound for Konominato Wharf from {{ill|Tōgō Station|ja|東郷駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōgō Station|qq=}} (Nishitetsu Bus Munakata); get off at the final stop. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakamiya Interchange|qq=}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koga Interchange|qq=}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Expressway|qq=}}. File:Oosimakou.jpg|Ōshima Port Ferry Terminal (2009) File:Munakata City Ferry Oshima.jpg|Ferry Oshima (2018) == References == == See Also == * {{ill|Geography of Japan|ja|日本の地理|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Geography of Japan|qq=}} * {{ill|List of islands of Japan|ja|日本の島の一覧|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of islands of Japan|qq=}} == External Links == {{Commonscat|Ōshima, Munakata}} * [https://maps.gsi.go.jp/#14/33.897741/130.433164/&base=std&ls=std&disp=1&vs=c1j0h0k0l0u0t0z0r0s0m0f1 GSI Maps] {{ill|Designated Islands of Japan|ja|日本の指定離島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Designated Islands of Japan|qq=}} {{Normdaten}} == References == [{{Geonameslink|gnid=1853774|name=o%20shima}} Ō Shima] at [{{Geonamesabout}} Geonames.org (cc-by)]; {{Location map|Japan |float=right |width=300 | caption = Location of Ō Shima in Japan. | label = Ō Shima|position=right|background=white|lat=33.90222|long=130.42414}} '''Ōshima''' (大島) is an {{ill|Island|ja|島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Island|qq=}} (an inhabited island) in {{ill|Munakata City|ja|宗像市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City|qq=}}, {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|ja|福岡県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefecture|qq=}}, facing the boundary between {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibiki-nada|qq=}} and {{ill|Genkai-nada|ja|玄界灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genkai-nada|qq=}}. As part of the Chikuzen Islands area, it is designated as a Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Area under the {{ill|Remote Islands Development Act|ja|離島振興法|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Remote Islands Development Act|qq=}}.[https://www.mlit.go.jp/kokudoseisaku/chirit/content/001619210.pdf Fukuoka Prefecture "Fukuoka Prefecture Remote Islands Development Plan (FY2023 – FY2032)"] – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (Accessed September 23, 2024) The island’s area is about 7.17 {{ill|square kilometers|ja|平方キロメートル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/square kilometers|qq=}}. It is also known as Chikuzen-Ōshima and is one of the {{ill|the Seven Inlets of Munakata|ja|宗像七浦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/the Seven Inlets of Munakata|qq=}}, home to the Middle Shrine (Nakatsumiya) of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}} and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho, which are part of a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Heritage Site|qq=}}. Its catchphrase is “Island that Protects the Gods.” == Overview == {{Created by bot|Lsjbot|Japan|date=2017-02}} :''For other places with the same name, see [[Ō Shima]].'' {{geobox | 1 = Island | name = Ō Shima | native_name = 大島 | other_name = Ō Sima | category = Island | etymology = | nickname = | image = | image_caption = | country = {{flag|Japan}} | country_flag = true | state = [[Fukuoka Prefecture]] | state_type = Prefecture | region = | region_type = | district = | district_type = | municipality = | municipality_type = | parent = | range = | range_type = Archipelago | border = | part = | city = | capital = | landmark = | river = | location = | lat_d = 33.90222 | lat_m = | lat_s = | lat_NS = | long_d = 130.42414 | long_m = | long_s = | long_EW = | highest = | highest_location = | highest_region = | highest_country = | highest_elevation = | highest_lat_d = | highest_lat_m = | highest_lat_s = | highest_lat_NS = | highest_long_d = | highest_long_m = | highest_long_s = | highest_long_EW = | length = | length_orientation = | width = | width_orientation = | height = | area = 7.46 | population = | population_date = | population_note = | population_density = | population_density_note = | public = | access = | timezone = [[Japan Standard Time|JST]] | utc_offset = +9 | timezone_DST = | utc_offset_DST = | postal_code = | area_code = | code = | free = | free_type = | map = | map_caption = | map_locator_x = | map_locator_y = | footnotes = | other_name1 = Ō-shima | other_name2 = 筑前大島 | other_name3 = Tchikuzen-Ōshima | elevation = 128 | timezone_label = Asia/Tokyo | geonames = 1853774 }} [[Island]] '''Ō Shima''' ([[Japanese]]: '''大島''', '''筑前大島''') is in [[Japan]]. It is located in the prefecture of [[Fukuoka Prefecture]], in the southwestern part of the country, about {{formatnum:900}} km west of [[Tokyo (the capital city of Japan)|Tokyo]], the capital of the country. It covers an area of approximately {{formatnum:7.5}} square kilometers. The terrain of Ō Shima is flat.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The highest point of the island is {{formatnum:206}} meters above sea level. It spans 3.1 km from north to south and 4.0 km from east to west.{{efn|group=saysay|Calculated from elevation data (DEM 3") from Viewfinder Panoramas. The full algorithm is available [https://sv.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Projekt_DotNetWikiBot_Framework/Lsjbot/Make-Geonames here].}} The climate is [[temperate]]. The average temperature is {{formatnum:15}} [[°C]]. The warmest month is August, at {{formatnum:24}} [[°C]], and the coldest is February, at {{formatnum:6}} °C. The average annual rainfall is {{formatnum:2130}} millimeters. The wettest month is July, with {{formatnum:410}} millimeters of rain, and the driest is January, with {{formatnum:47}} millimeters. {| class="climate chart" |- | '''Ō Shima Climate Data''' | January | 5 | 8 | 47 | February | 4 | 7 | 157| March | 6 | 13 | 136| April | 10 | 17 | 120| May | 14 | 20 | 89| June | 15 | 21 | 294| July | 20 | 22 | 410| August | 23 | 26 | 383| September | 19 | 21 | 146| October | 17 | 21 | 126| November | 12 | 16 | 124| December | 7 | 11 | 98|- | colspan="13" | Data source: |} == Geography == [[File:Oshima_Island,_Munakata_Fukuoka_Aerial_photograph.2010.jpg|alt=Ōshima aerial photograph.|thumb|280x280px]]
Created by combining 26 images taken on June 3, 2010. {{ill|GSI Aerial Photograph|ja|国土航空写真|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/GSI Aerial Photograph|qq=}}. Ōshima is located about 6.5 {{ill|kilometers|ja|キロメートル|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/kilometers|qq=}} northwest of the Konominato Port on the Munakata mainland. About 5 km to the east lies {{ill|Jinoshima|ja|地島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jinoshima|qq=}}. Together with Jinoshima and {{ill|Okinoshima|ja|沖ノ島|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okinoshima|qq=}}, it marks the boundary between {{ill|Genkai Sea|ja|玄界灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Genkai Sea|qq=}} and {{ill|Hibiki-nada|ja|響灘|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hibiki-nada|qq=}}—the sea on the west side of the island is Genkai-nada, and on the east side is Hibiki-nada. Its total area is 7.17 km{{sup|2}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.mlit.go.jp/common/001015648.pdf List of Remote Islands Development Countermeasure Implementation Areas]}} – Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, National and Regional Policy Bureau, Remote Islands Development Division, making it the largest of the remote islands in Fukuoka Prefecture. Much of the island is hilly with steep terrain, and the highest peak is Mitake (224 m) in the island’s center. On the eastern side of the island is Ōshima Port, where ferries connect to the mainland, and a ferry terminal is located there. Slightly south of the ferry terminal is Ōshima Fishing Port, while Miyazaki Fishing Port is to the northeast. Homes and settlements are concentrated around these port areas. The population is 540 with 278 households (from the Reiwa 2 {{ill|National Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本)|lt=National Census|lt_ja=国勢調査|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Census (Japan)|qq=}}). The island has {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|qq=}}, a {{ill|compulsory education school|ja|義務教育学校|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/compulsory education school|qq=}}. == History == In [[1889]] (Meiji 22), under the {{ill|Town and Village Act|ja|町村制|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Town and Village Act|qq=}}, it became {{ill|Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島村 (福岡県)|lt=Oshima Village|lt_ja=大島村|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oshima Village (Fukuoka Prefecture)|qq=}} in {{ill|Munakata District|ja|宗像郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata District|qq=}}. From May 27 to 28, 1905, the {{ill|Battle of Tsushima|ja|日本海海戦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Battle of Tsushima|qq=}} took place offshore, and many Russian soldiers’ bodies washed ashore on Ōshima.[https://news.yahoo.co.jp/byline/kodamakatsuya/20131103-00029474/ Katsuya Kodama “Memorial Service for the Russo-Japanese War on Munakata City’s Ōshima ~A New Bridge of Friendship and Peace between Japan and Russia!~” (November 3, 2013)] (Accessed January 16, 2018) Residents are said to have buried them respectfully. On March 28, 2005, the village was merged into Munakata City. Beginning in 1935 (Shōwa 10), as part of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimonoseki Fortress|qq=}}, a battery was constructed on the island’s northern coast (Ōshima Battery) equipped with four {{ill|Type 45 15 cm Cannon|ja|四五式十五糎加農砲|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Type 45 15 cm Cannon|qq=}}. Associated facilities included an observation post, underground ammunition depot, a mobile 150 cm searchlight, and a power station. After the war, these cannons were removed, but their mounts and other remnants remain. Since 2012, a Japan–Russia joint memorial service has been held for those who died in the Battle of Tsushima, and in November 2013, a monument to the war dead was erected in front of the former Ōshima Battery. In July 2017 ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Heisei|qq=}} 29), Nakatsumiya and the Okitsumiya Yohaisho were inscribed as part of the “{{ill|Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|ja|「神宿る島」宗像・沖ノ島と関連遺産群|1=Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|13=User:Immanuelle/Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region|qq=}}” World Heritage Site. == Religious Facilities == At the summit of Mt. Mitake stands an observation platform and the Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) of Nakatsumiya, called {{ill|Mitake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitake Shrine|qq=}}. In ancient times, this was a ritual site for Nakatsumiya. Nearby is the Orihime-Hikoboshi Shrine, and local tradition holds that this place is the birthplace of Japan’s Tanabata legend. Near the port is Nakatsumiya of {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}}, dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the {{ill|The Three Female Deities of Munakata|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/The Three Female Deities of Munakata|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=}}. On the north side of the island is the {{ill|Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|ja|沖津宮遙拝所|lt=Okitsumiya Yohaisho|lt_ja=沖津宮遙拝所|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okitsu-miya Yohaisho|qq=}}, where one can worship the distant island of Okinoshima, home to Okitsumiya, which is forbidden to women. On clear days, one can faintly see Okinoshima from there, but it cannot be seen on cloudy or rainy days. These two sites are part of the “Sacred Island of Okinoshima and Associated Sites in the Munakata Region,” a {{ill|World Heritage Site|ja|世界遺産|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/World Heritage Site|qq=}}. Additionally, Ōshima is traditionally said to be the place where {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Munetō|qq=}} spent his final years in exile. It is also on the route of the {{ill|Kyushu Olle|ja|九州オルレ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Olle|qq=}} hiking course. == Major Facilities and Attractions on the Island == === Main Facilities === * Municipal Office – Munakata City Ōshima Administrative Center * School – {{ill|Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|ja|宗像市立大島学園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata City Oshima Gakuen|qq=}} * Nursery – Ōshima Nursery School === Tourist Attractions === * Umingu Ōshima – A marine experience facility offering {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fishing|qq=}} and {{ill|Sea kayaking|ja|シーカヤック|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sea kayaking|qq=}}. * {{ill|Munakata Taisha|ja|宗像大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Taisha|qq=}} Nakatsumiya – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. Dedicated to Tagitsu-hime, the second of the Munakata Three Sisters. * {{ill|Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|ja|御嶽神社 (宗像市)|lt=Mitake Shrine|lt_ja=御嶽神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitake Shrine (Munakata City)|qq=}} – The Okunomiya (Inner Shrine) and original sacred site of Nakatsumiya from ancient times, known as the Ōshima Mitake Archaeological Site. * Mt. Mitake – The highest peak on the island, home to Mitake Shrine at its summit. The summit has an observation platform. * Grave of {{ill|Abe no Munetō|ja|安倍宗任|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe no Munetō|qq=}} – According to tradition, Munetō was exiled here and spent his final days on the island. * Yume-no-Sayoshima – A small island covered by pines on the east side of Ōshima. In the Muromachi period, the {{ill|Renga poet|ja|連歌師|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Renga poet|qq=}} {{ill|Iio Sōgi|ja|宗祇|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iio Sōgi|qq=}} visited and composed waka poetry about it. It is accessible only at low tide. * Kansu Beach – A swimming beach near Yume-no-Sayoshima. * Ōshima Exchange Hall (Ōshima Kōryūkan) – A facility introducing the history and culture of Ōshima and Okinoshima. * Okitsumiya Yohaisho – Part of the Munakata Taisha World Heritage Site. A {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=worship site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haisho|qq=}} for the sacred island of Okinoshima, the location of Okitsumiya. * Windmill Observation Deck – Known as one of the best scenic spots on the island. On clear days, Okinoshima is visible. * Ōshima Battery Ruins of the {{ill|Shimonoseki Fortress|ja|下関要塞|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimonoseki Fortress|qq=}} – Near the Windmill Observation Deck. Remnants include an underground ammunition depot and observation post. The Battle of Tsushima War Dead Memorial stands here. * Ōshima Ranch – Next to the Windmill Observation Deck. Offers horseback riding experiences. * Kamizaki – A cape in the island’s northwest. A monument established by the former {{ill|Ministry of the Army|ja|陸軍省|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of the Army|qq=}} stands at the tip. * Batei Rock (Horseshoe Rock) – Located at Kamizaki. Its name comes from a legend in which the Munakata Deity rode a horse and flew among the islands. Numerous cup marks are found on the rock. * Ōshima Lighthouse – A white lighthouse near Kamizaki, known for its scenic views. * Miura Cave – A cave near Ōshima Lighthouse, associated with a {{ill|Hidden Christian|ja|隠れキリシタン|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hidden Christian|qq=}} legend. File:Umingu Oshima.jpg|Umingu Ōshima File:Street view near Oshima Port on Oshima Island, Munakata, Fukuoka.JPG|Townscape near Ōshima Port File:Grand torii of Munakata Grand Shrine (Nakatsu Shrine).JPG|Torii of Munakata Taisha Nakatsumiya File:Abe no Muneto tomb.jpg|Grave of Abe no Munetō File:Yumenosayoshima and Kansu Beach.jpg|Yume-no-Sayoshima File:Oshima Culture Center.jpg|Ōshima Exchange Hall File:宗像大社沖津宮遙拝所 - panoramio.jpg|Okitsumiya Yohaisho (Munakata Taisha) File:大島灯台 - panoramio.jpg|Ōshima Lighthouse File:Kamizaki Oshima.jpg|Kamizaki === Accommodations === There are a few inns and guesthouses on the island. A campground called Ōshima Campground is located on the island’s western coast. == Festivals == * {{ill|Miare Festival|ja|みあれ祭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miare Festival|qq=}} – The autumn grand festival of Munakata Taisha, marking the beginning of the Tashima Hōjōe (harvest festival). It is the one time of the year when all three goddesses are enshrined together. == Industry == {{ill|Fishing|ja|釣り|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fishing|qq=}} is the main industry, but small-scale {{ill|Agriculture|ja|農業|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agriculture|qq=}} also exists, and specialty products include {{ill|Amanatsu|ja|甘夏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanatsu|qq=}}, {{ill|Akamoku|ja|アカモク|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akamoku|qq=}}, and {{ill|Sea salt|ja|海塩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sea salt|qq=}}. In addition, {{ill|Japanese Black|ja|黒毛和種|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Black|qq=}} cattle are raised on the western side of the island at Ōshima Ranch. == Transportation == === Land Transportation === {{ill|Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|ja|福岡県道541号大島循環線|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuoka Prefectural Route 541 Oshima Circular Line|qq=}} runs around the central settlement area near the ferry terminal in the southeast and circles the interior of the island, with additional roads leading into the central settlement and coastal areas. Two sightseeing buses operate around the island: the “Granshima-ru” (run by {{ill|Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|ja|西鉄バス宗像|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitetsu Bus Munakata|qq=}}) and the “Miare-gō” (operated by Minato Taxi). In April 2008, Minato Taxi set up an office on the island with two taxis (currently one), usually stationed at the ferry terminal. Bicycle rentals are also available at the ferry terminal and elsewhere. === Maritime Transportation === From the mainland’s Konominato Port in Munakata City to {{ill|Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|ja|大島港 (福岡県)|lt=Ōshima Port|lt_ja=大島港|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōshima Port (Fukuoka Prefecture)|qq=}}, it takes 25 minutes on the municipal ferry “{{ill|Munakata Municipal Ferry|ja|宗像市営渡船|lt=Ferry Oshima|lt_ja=フェリーおおしま|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Municipal Ferry|qq=}}” or 15 minutes on the passenger boat “Shiokaze.” The schedule and current operating status are posted on Munakata City’s website. There are also private sea taxis. To reach Konominato Port, take the bus bound for Konominato Wharf from {{ill|Tōgō Station|ja|東郷駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōgō Station|qq=}} (Nishitetsu Bus Munakata); get off at the final stop. By car, it is about 19 km from the {{ill|Wakamiya Interchange|ja|若宮インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakamiya Interchange|qq=}} or 17 km from the {{ill|Koga Interchange|ja|古賀インターチェンジ|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Koga Interchange|qq=}} on the {{ill|Kyushu Expressway|ja|九州自動車道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyushu Expressway|qq=}}.
